[11:48] Customer: just wondering for the future
[11:48] Customer: totally hypothetical lol im not going anywhere rn
[11:49] Customer: but if I moved to Denver would I need to change anything on the card?
[11:49] Customer: like would i have to get a whole new card account or something
[11:50] Agent (Anjali): That's a very practical question, not random at all! And to answer it, no, you would not need to get a new card or a new account. Your Amazon Prime Visa (*3810) account would remain exactly the same.

[11:51] Customer: thats easy enough then

[11:52] Agent (Anjali): I completely understand. We hear that from customers from time to time. We'll be here to help update your address if that day ever comes!
[11:53] Agent (Anjali): Was there anything else I could assist you with today, Ms. Park? Any other questions about your card or your account?
[11:53] Customer: no i think that was everything
[11:54] Customer: you were a big help
[11:54] Customer: ty anjali
[11:54] Agent (Anjali): It has been my pleasure assisting you, Nadia. Thank you for choosing us and for using Secure Chat. I hope you have a wonderful rest of your day!
[11:55] Agent (Anjali): This chat session will now end.

cust_synth_028:C06.body:
IVR: Thank you for calling Premier Financial. Your call may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance. To report a card lost or stolen, press 1. For card services, including activation, payments, and balance inquiries, press 2. For all other inquiries, press 3, or stay on the line to speak with the next available representative.
[BEEP]
IVR: You have selected card services. To activate a new card, press 1. To make a payment, press 2. For balance and transaction information, press 3. To dispute a transaction, press 4. To return to the main menu, press 9.

[BEEP]

IVR: Please have your card and personal information ready. All of our representatives are currently assisting other customers. Your call is important to us. Please remain on the line. Your estimated wait time is... four minutes.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can manage your account twenty-four seven online at premierfinancial.com? Check your balance, make payments, and even lock your card, all from the comfort of your home. Ask your representative about enrolling in online services today. Premier Financial. Your partner in prosperity.

[upbeat instrumental music plays for 90 seconds]

AGENT: Thank you for holding, you've reached Premier Financial Card Services. My name is Dana. How can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: Hi Dana. Yes, I need to activate a new card they sent me.

AGENT: Absolutely, I can definitely help with that. To get started, could I please have your first and last name?

CUSTOMER: Nadia Park.

AGENT: Thank you, Nadia. And just to pull up your account, I'll need to verify a few more details. I'm going to send a one-time passcode to the mobile number we have on file. Can you read that back to me when you receive it?

CUSTOMER: Oh, um. I don't have my phone on me right now, I'm at my desk at work. I'm calling from my office landline. Is there another way?

AGENT: Not a problem at all, we can use some other information. Can I get your home city and state?

CUSTOMER: Austin, Texas.

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. And could you please verify the last four digits of your Social Security Number?

CUSTOMER: It's [REDACTED].

AGENT: Got it. And finally for me, your date of birth?

CUSTOMER: [REDACTED].

AGENT: Excellent. Thank you so much for that, Ms. Park. I have your account pulled up here. Okay, so you're calling to activate a new card. I see we recently ordered a replacement for your Amazon Prime Visa card ending in three-eight-one-zero. Is that the one?

CUSTOMER: Yes, the new one they mailed me. It just came today.

AGENT: Great. Can you read the last four digits of the new card number to me?

CUSTOMER: Yes, hold on. Let me get it out of the envelope. It's uh... one-three-three-seven.

AGENT: Okay, one-three-three-seven. Thank you. Just one moment while I pull that up in the system. Okay... So, I'm just going to start the activation process. This will deactivate your old card, the one ending in thirty-eight ten, and your new card will be ready for use immediately. Does that sound good?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that's fine. The old one, the chip stopped working anyway. That's why I had to get a new one.

AGENT: Ah, yes I see the note here from the branch visit. That's definitely a hassle, I'm glad the new one arrived for you quickly. Okay, just give me one...

CUSTOMER: You know, actually, while I have you on the line. I'm supposed to be getting a call back from a supervisor about something else. It's been... gosh, it must be over a month now. I never heard from anyone.

AGENT: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. A supervisor callback? Let me see if I can find any information on that for you. Do you remember roughly when you requested it, or what it was about?

CUSTOMER: It was... April. Sometime in mid-April. I called about a... a credit on my account. A dispute I had filed. The credit had posted, but I had some questions about it, and the person I was speaking with couldn't answer them, so she said she'd have a supervisor call me back. I even gave her this number, my work number, specifically.

AGENT: Okay, I'm looking at your contact history now. I see a call from you on... let's see... April 12th regarding a dispute. Is that the one?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that sounds right. It was for three hundred and something dollars.

AGENT: Okay, I see the notes here from my colleague. It says you were calling to confirm a provisional credit of three hundred thirteen dollars and eighty-nine cents had been applied for dispute number DSP-1480747.

CUSTOMER: That's the one. And I had questions, and she said she'd have someone call me. My brother was even here, Emeka, he heard the whole thing, he was getting so annoyed for me. I gave her the number, I remember because I had to correct her, she read it back wrong the first time. I gave her 412-555-0567.

AGENT: Yes, I see that callback number noted right here in the file. Let me just read through the rest of the notes from that interaction... one moment. [typing sounds] Hmm. This is... I'm very sorry, Ms. Park. I see the whole summary of the conversation about the dispute, and I see the callback number was recorded, but there's no entry here that a supervisor callback was actually requested or escalated. There's no task created for it.

CUSTOMER: What? So she just... didn't do it?

I would recommend you monitor your transactions in the app or online for the next few days very carefully. If you see any other suspicious activity, even for a very small amount, call us back immediately and we will close the card right away.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I can do that. That's a relief, I hate having to update all my automatic payments.

AGENT: I completely understand. It's a huge hassle. Okay, I have the dispute filed now. I have two reference numbers for you. Are you able to write these down?

CUSTOMER: Uh, yes. Let me just grab a pen. Okay, go ahead.

AGENT: The first number is the dispute number, which is tied directly to that specific charge. It's DSP-1480747. I'll repeat that. D as in David, S as in Sam, P as in Paul, dash, one, four, eight, zero, seven, four, seven.

AGENT: Okay one four eight zero seven four seven. Got it.

CUSTOMER: And the second number?

AGENT: Yes, the second one is the overall case number for our conversation and the actions we've taken today. That one is CASE-6327908. That's C, A, S, E, dash, six, three, two, seven, nine, zero, eight.

CUSTOMER: Okay... 6327908. Got it. So, what happens now? Does the charge get taken off my account?

AGENT: So, what happens now is the investigation process begins. We will reach out to the merchant's bank to get more information about the charge. In the meantime, you should see a provisional credit for the full amount of three hundred thirteen dollars and eighty-nine cents post to your account.

CUSTOMER: Oh good. When will that happen?

AGENT: That process isn't instant, it does take a little bit of time for the system to post it. It usually posts within ten business days, sometimes much sooner, but that's the standard timeframe we provide. So you may still see the charge on your account for a little while, but a matching credit will appear to balance it out while we investigate.

CUSTOMER: Okay, ten business days. And what if this... [crosstalk] florist place says I did buy it?

AGENT: Sorry, go ahead?

CUSTOMER: I was just saying, what if they lie and say the charge is real?

AGENT: That's what the investigation is for. We give the merchant a deadline to respond and provide compelling evidence that the charge is legitimate. This would be something like a signed receipt, proof of delivery to your address, or an IP address match for an online order, something that ties you to the purchase. CUSTOMER: July 2, 2026. Okay.

CUSTOMER: Okay. That makes sense. It's just so weird. I have no idea how they would have even gotten my card number. It's kind of scary.

AGENT: I completely understand your concern, Ms. Park. It's unsettling, for sure. Again, please keep a close eye on your account activity and report anything that looks even slightly out of place.

CUSTOMER: I will. Definitely. So, just to be clear, I don't have to do anything else right now? Just wait for the credit and watch my account?

AGENT: That is exactly right. You've done your part by reporting it to us. We will handle the rest of the investigation from here. Is there anything else I can assist you with today, Ms. Park? Maybe look into that travel rewards card for you?

CUSTOMER: [laughs] No, no thank you. I think that's enough excitement for one day. You've been very helpful, Rafael. I appreciate it.

AGENT: It's my pleasure, Ms. Park. Thank you again for calling, and please don't hesitate to call us back if anything else comes up. Have a wonderful rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye.

AGENT: Goodbye.

cust_synth_028:C05.body:
Cx Nadia Park in branch approx 2:15pm. No appointment, was a walk-in. Looked like a short wait, maybe five minutes. Seemed a little frazzled when she came up to my desk.

Pulled up her profile in CCK. Full identity verification performed using her Texas driver's license. Photo matched, address matched the Austin, TX address on file. All good to proceed.

Primary issue for visit: problem with her Amazon Prime Visa card (*3810).
- Per cx, the card's chip has stopped reading correctly at payment terminals.
- This has been happening for about a week. She says she inserts the card and the machine just beeps with a "chip read error" or something similar.
- The cashier then has to instruct her to swipe it.
- She says the magstripe swipe works most of the time, but it failed once entirely at a small cafe and she had to use a different bank's card, which she said was "a bit embarrassing."
- Main frustration for her is that the Amazon card is her primary card for everything, to maximize her points.
- I empathized, told her we see this happen from time to time. The chips can get scratched or demagnetized, or sometimes they just fail. Assured her it's a simple fix.

While reviewing her account in the platform to get to the card services screen, I saw the notes from her contacts earlier in the year.
- I asked her casually, "Hey, I see a note here from a little while back, looks like you had a question about a charge from a florist? Did that all get resolved to your satisfaction?"
- She thought for a second and then said, "Oh, the Harbor Lights charge! Yes, that was so strange. My brother Emeka actually caught it. But yeah, I saw the bank credited my account back, so I think we're all good on that. Thanks for asking."
- Good to hear that was sorted. Closed the loop.

Okay, so proceeding with the card replacement.
- Advised her the best and only real option is for us to issue a replacement card. It's free of charge for a damaged card.
- She agreed immediately. "Yes, please. Let's do it."
- Navigated to the card services module. System was a bit laggy today, which is pretty standard for a weekday afternoon. Apologized for the delay while the pages loaded.
- First step was to confirm all her contact info before placing the order.
- Verbally confirmed her mailing address in Austin, she said it was correct.
- Then I moved to the email address. I read it aloud: "And the best email for you is nadia.park51@example.org?"
- She laughed a little. "Yes, that's the one. I'm glad you read it back. I just changed it not too long ago and I'm still getting used to it myself. I think I even typed it wrong when I was changing it over chat, so now I'm paranoid about it." Confirmed correct.

Processed the order.
- I explained she had two options for delivery: standard mail at no cost, which takes 5-7 business days, or expedited shipping for a fee.
- She opted for standard mail. Said there was no major rush.
- I made sure to be very clear on the next part. I explained that her current card, the one ending in *3810, will NOT be deactivated immediately. It will continue to function for online purchases and for magstripe swipes until she receives and activates the new card.
- She was relieved to hear that. "Oh good, so I'm not totally stuck."
- She asked if the card number would stay the same. I explained that b/c this is a replacement for a physically faulty card, we issue a new card number for security and tracking purposes. Her new card number would be different.
- Advised her the new card will be the one ending in *1337.
- I repeated this for clarity. "So in about a week, you'll receive a new Amazon Prime Visa ending in *1337. There will be a sticker on it with an activation phone number. As soon as you call and activate that new card, your old *3810 will automatically be shut off."
- She nodded. She asked a good question about her recurring payments. I advised her that yes, once the new card *1337 is activated, she will need to update her payment information on any sites where the old card is saved, like for her Prime membership itself. She took out her phone to make a note.

While the order was submitting, I had the account overview screen up.
- I noticed her perfect payment history, no late payments ever. As a matter of course, and b/c I had the fee schedule window open from my last cx, I did the standard disclosure.
- "And Ms. Park, just as a general notification while I have the official fee schedule on my screen, our policy for this card account is that late payment fees can be up to $41.00. Obviously, that's not something you need to worry about with your excellent history, it's just a standard informational point we mention during account service." She just nodded.

Okay, the order went through. I copied the confirmation details from the system into this write-up for the official record.
CARD REPLACEMENT ORDER SUBMITTED. ACCT: ...XXXX3810. NEW CARD: ...XXXX1337. DELIVERY: STANDARD MAIL 5-7 BUSINESS DAYS. STATUS: PENDING FULFILLMENT. REASON CODE: DAMAGED/WORN CARD. NO FEE.

We had another minute while the system generated a reference number.
- I asked her what brought her to our area, since her profile says Austin. She said she's just visiting family for a couple of weeks.
- I saw the 412 area code for her callback number, 412-555-0567, and asked if she was originally from Pittsburgh.
- She said her company is headquartered there, so she has a work line based there that just forwards to her cell. Said she works fully remote from Austin. She added, "I have to be careful when I give that number out, I think I almost gave the wrong one to one of your colleagues on the phone last month, I get the last two digits swapped sometimes." This confirms the number on file is the one she wants us to use.

Wrapped up the visit.
- I summarized the key points one last time: New card (*1337) coming in 5-7 business days, old card (*3810) works via swipe/online until then.
- Provided her with a printout of the service summary with my name, the branch address, and the interaction reference number.
- She was very appreciative and thanked me for making it easy.
- Cx left the branch around 2:40pm.

Follow-up:
- No immediate f/u required from branch.
- Cx is fully aware of the timeline and the activation process for the new card *1337.
- Advised her to call the number on the back of her card if the replacement hasn't arrived within 10 business days.
- Wes.

cust_synth_028:C03.body:
IVR: Thank you for calling Premier OmniBank. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. To continue in English, press one. Para Español, oprima dos.

IVR: Please listen carefully as our menu options have recently changed. For account balances or recent transactions, press one. To report a card lost or stolen, press two. For questions about your Amazon Prime Visa card, including rewards or disputes, press three. To speak to a representative about loans or mortgages, press four. For all other inquiries, press zero.

IVR: Please say or enter the last four digits of your Social Security Number.

IVR: Thank you. Please wait while we connect you to the next available agent.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can manage your account 24/7 online at premieromnibank.com? Check balances, pay bills, and even deposit checks all from your computer or mobile device. Ask your representative about setting up online access today. We appreciate your patience.

AGENT: Thank you for holding, my name is David. I see you're calling from Austin. How can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: Hi David. Yes, I'm calling to check on a dispute. I filed it a while back and I got a credit, but I just want to understand what the next steps are.

AGENT: Okay, I can certainly try to help with that. Do you have the dispute number handy?

CUSTOMER: Um, let me see. I wrote it down somewhere… hang on. It’s on a sticky note here. Okay, it’s DSP, I think… dash… one four eight zero seven four seven.

AGENT: Got it. DSP-1480747. Let me pull that up for you. Just one moment while my system loads. Can I just confirm your full name for the record?

CUSTOMER: Nadia Park.

AGENT: Thank you, Ms. Park. Okay, I see the dispute here for a charge of $313.89. And you're calling about the provisional credit that was applied?

CUSTOMER: Yes, exactly. I saw it posted, um, let's see… it was the day before yesterday. And I just wanted to know if that means it’s all done. Is the case closed?

AGENT: Right, I see the credit here for $313.89. So, the provisional credit is just a temporary credit we provide while we investigate the claim with the merchant. It doesn't mean the dispute is finalized. The investigation is still ongoing.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Okay. So how long does that usually take? It’s been over a month since I first called about this.

AGENT: I understand. These investigations can sometimes take a while, up to two full billing cycles in some cases, depending on how responsive the merchant is.

CUSTOMER: Two billing cycles? Wow. I was really hoping to have this resolved.

AGENT: I can see that the case is with our specialized back-office team. Unfortunately, I don't have a direct timeline I can give you from my system. They handle all the communication with the merchant.

CUSTOMER: So there’s no one I can talk to who would know more? I feel a little bit in the dark here.

AGENT: I can transfer you over to the disputes department. They have a bit more visibility into the case notes than I do. Would you like me to do that?

CUSTOMER: Yes, please. That would be great.

AGENT: Okay, Ms. Park. I'm going to place you on a brief hold while I connect you. Please don't hang up.

HOLD MESSAGE: Your financial security is our top priority. Premier OmniBank uses state-of-the-art encryption and fraud monitoring to protect your accounts. Never share your PIN or online banking password with anyone. We will never call you and ask for this information.

AGENT: Hi, thank you for holding. My name is Keisha, and I'm a specialist in the disputes department. I see you were speaking with David. How can I help you?

CUSTOMER: Hi Keisha. Yes, he was transferring me. I'm calling to check on the status of a dispute, number DSP-1480747.

AGENT: Okay, let me just get that pulled up here. One moment… Okay, Ms. Park, I have your account. I'm just reviewing the notes from David. So, you're calling about a charge for $313.89 from a furniture store, is that correct?

CUSTOMER: No, that’s not right. It was a florist. Harbor Lights Florist. I called about it back in early March.

AGENT: Oh, my apologies. Thank you for clarifying. I see that now in the original notes. Florist. Got it. And you saw the provisional credit post to your account and wanted to know if the case was closed.

CUSTOMER: That’s right. It posted the day before yesterday. I just have no idea what to expect. Am I going to get a letter? An email? How will I know when it’s actually over?

AGENT: That's a very fair question, Ms. Park. I can confirm the investigation is still open. The merchant has a set period of time to respond to our inquiry and provide evidence that the charge is valid. If they don't respond, or if their evidence isn't sufficient, the dispute is typically found in your favor and the provisional credit becomes permanent.

CUSTOMER: And if they do respond?

AGENT: If they provide compelling evidence, like a signed receipt or proof of delivery to your address, we would review it. In that situation, the credit might be reversed, but you would be notified before that happens and have an opportunity to provide more information.

CUSTOMER: This is all so complicated. I’m hoping to get it sorted out before I go on a trip in a few weeks, just to have one less thing to worry about.

AGENT: I can definitely understand that. Traveling can be stressful enough. Are you going somewhere nice?

CUSTOMER: Just visiting some family abroad. It’ll be good to see them.

AGENT: That sounds lovely. Well, just as a helpful tip while we’re on the topic, remember that if you use your Amazon Prime Visa card at an ATM overseas, it’s treated as a cash advance. That comes with a $12.00 fee per withdrawal and the interest starts accruing from day one at 30.24%, so it's usually better to use it for purchases directly.

CUSTOMER: Oh, wow. Okay, that is good to know. Thank you. But back to this dispute… is there really nothing you can tell me about the timeline? It just feels like it's in a black hole. Hold on one second, my brother is waving at me. What?

EMEKA: Is that the bank? Are you still dealing with that?

CUSTOMER: Yes, I’m trying to figure out what’s going on.

EMEKA: Let me talk to them. Hello? Ma'am?

AGENT: Hello, this is Keisha.

EMEKA: Hi Keisha. I’m Nadia’s brother, Emeka. Listen, I told her she should have just cancelled the whole card when this happened. I had an issue with my card last year, the one ending in 5044, and they sorted it right out. You guys should just fix this for her. It’s been forever. If you need to call me about it to get it sorted, my number is 412-555-0366.

AGENT: I appreciate your concern, sir, but for privacy and security reasons, I can only discuss the account details with the primary account holder, Ms. Park.

CUSTOMER: Emeka, it's fine. Let me handle it. Thank you.

EMEKA: Alright, alright. Just trying to help.

CUSTOMER: Sorry about that, Keisha. He means well.

AGENT: Not a problem at all, Ms. Park. I completely understand. Now, where were we? Ah, the timeline. As I said, I can't give you a definite date, but what I can do is look into it further for you. I can see you've been waiting for an update for some time. I can open a new follow-up case right now to have a supervisor review the current status and see if we can get a clearer picture for you.

CUSTOMER: A supervisor? Would they be able to tell me more?

AGENT: They have access to a few more tools and can sometimes reach out directly to the analyst handling the claim. They can at least look at it and make sure it’s progressing as it should be.

CUSTOMER: Okay. Yes, I would appreciate that.

AGENT: Perfect. And what would be the best number for the supervisor to reach you at? I don't see a callback number noted on your file from today.

CUSTOMER: Oh, yes. You can call my office landline. That’s the best place to find me during the day. The number is 412-555-0576. Wait, no, hang on, that’s the main line. My direct extension is different. Sorry, it’s 412-555-0567.

AGENT: Okay, thank you for clarifying. Let me read that back to you. The best number is four one two, five five five, oh five six seven. Is that correct?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s it. 412-555-0567.

AGENT: Excellent. I've added that to the file. And I am opening a new case for you right now for this request. The reference number for today’s call and this follow-up is CASE-5599947.

CUSTOMER: Okay… CASE-5599947. Got it.

AGENT: I am putting in the request right now for a supervisor to review dispute DSP-1480747 and provide you with an update on the investigation timeline. I will make sure this is marked as a priority. I'm going to promise you that a supervisor will call back on the number you just provided. You can expect that call by Friday.

CUSTOMER: By Friday? Okay. That sounds good. Thank you, Keisha. I appreciate you taking the time to do that.

AGENT: You are most welcome, Ms. Park. It’s the least I can do. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, that’s everything. Just waiting for that call.

AGENT: Alright. Well, thank you again for calling Premier OmniBank. I hope you have a wonderful trip, and please don't hesitate to call back if anything else comes up.

CUSTOMER: Thank you. You too. Bye.

cust_synth_028:C11.body:
Customer came into the branch today, Nadia Park. I remembered her name but pulled up her profile just to be sure. Very pleasant lady. She’s one of our Austin-based customers, so it was nice to see her in her home branch. We started with the usual verification. She had her driver's license ready to go, and I also had her enter her PIN on the pad for dual-factor auth. Everything matched up.

CUST AUTHENTICATED VIA ID AND PIN. VERIFIED ALL CONTACT INFO ON PROFILE.

I confirmed her details, noting the new callback number she added a little while back, the 412-555-0996 number. She said, "Oh, good, I'm glad that went through. That's my work desk phone, it's just easier to reach me there during the day." I also confirmed her email is park.n56@example.org, and she said yes, that's the one she's using now. Seems like she had a couple of old ones on the profile from way back but the primary is correct.

She said she needed a cashier's check. She's moving apartments (still within Austin, she loves it here) and the new landlord is old school and wants a certified payment for the security deposit and first month's rent. We talked for a minute about the crazy rental market here. She said she was just happy to find a place that allowed her dog, a little corgi.

So, I started the process for the cashier's check, pulling the funds from her primary checking. As I was getting the system to process it, she got a little quiet and then said she had a different kind of question. She was almost hesitant to ask. She leaned in a little and said she was thinking about simplifying her finances, and was curious what the process would be if she ever wanted to close her account with us. She immediately followed it up with, "I am NOT closing the account, I just want to know what the steps would be." She said it three or four times. "I'm not doing it now, I promise. Just thinking ahead. A friend of mine is moving overseas and had to close all her accounts and it was a whole thing, so it got me thinking about my own."

I assured her it was a totally normal question and that I was happy to walk her through the hypothetical process. I explained that we would first need to make sure all pending transactions were cleared and that the balance was at zero. We'd have to transfer any remaining funds out, either as cash if she was in the branch, or via a transfer to an external account, or we could issue a final cashier's check. I mentioned that any automatic payments or direct deposits linked to the account would need to be rerouted by her well in advance to avoid any returns or missed payments. We also talked about any linked credit cards, like her Amazon Prime Visa, and how closing the checking account wouldn't automatically close the card. Her card ending in  1337 would remain active.

She nodded along, seeming to find it all very reasonable. She said, "That makes sense. It's really about the autopayments, isn't it? That's the part that seems like a headache." I agreed and said that's where we see the most issues when people decide to close accounts without planning. I told her we'd obviously be sad to see her go if she ever did, especially since she's been a customer for a while and seems to be getting good value from the card benefits. I mentioned that it's a great card for everyday spending, and reminded her about the current promo for 5x points on dining, just in case she wasn't aware. She laughed and said, "Don't worry, you're not getting rid of me that easily. You guys have been really helpful." She then brought up that issue she had with a flower shop a few months ago, and how grateful she was that our disputes team was able to get her money back. She said that kind of service is why she's planning on staying.

After we finished talking about the 'what-if' scenario, she seemed relieved, like she'd just been mentally tidying up. She then switched back to the original topic. "Okay, sorry for the tangent! Now, for that check..." She gave me the name of the property management company to make the check payable to. I confirmed the amount with her one more time before printing. While the check was printing, I made a bit of small talk. I saw the note on her file about the travel notice for Dublin that was later canceled. I asked, "I know you were supposed to take a trip to Ireland a while back, did you ever get to reschedule it?" She sighed and said no, not yet. Her friend who she was supposed to go with had a family emergency, so they had to postpone it indefinitely. She said they're hoping to try again next year, maybe in the spring.

I handed her the cashier's check and the receipt. She tucked it into her purse and thanked me for all the help. She said she felt much better just knowing what the process for things were, even if she wasn't going to do them. She was very appreciative and friendly throughout the entire interaction.

Follow-up:
No follow-up action required. Customer was inquiring about the account closure process for informational purposes only and explicitly stated she does not intend to close any accounts. Provided information on cashier's check as requested. Customer left satisfied.

IVR: Okay. Connecting you to the next available agent.

HOLD MESSAGE: We appreciate your patience. Did you know you can manage most account services, including reporting a lost or stolen card, right from the Chase mobile app? Download it today from your app store. With the Chase Freedom Flex card, every purchase brings you closer to your next adventure. Right now, earn 75,000 bonus points after you spend four thousand dollars on purchases in the first three months from account opening. That's nine hundred dollars toward your next trip. Ask your representative for more details.

AGENT: Thank you for holding, my name is Grace. I'm with the Fraud Prevention department. How can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, finally. My name is Marcus Lindqvist. I've been trying to get through the robot menu for five minutes.

AGENT: I do apologize for the wait times today, Mr. Lindquist. I can definitely help you now that you're through. For security, I just need to verify your identity. Can you please confirm the city and state you have on file with us?

CUSTOMER: It's Lindqvist, with a V. And yes, it's Atlanta, Georgia.

AGENT: My apologies, Mr. Lindqvist. Thank you. And could you tell me the email address associated with your account?

CUSTOMER: Sure, it's marcusl, the letter l, then three one, at example dot net.

AGENT: Perfect, thank you so much for verifying that information for me. I see you're fully verified now. So, how can I assist you with your account today?

CUSTOMER: Right, so I was just looking at my recent statement for my... uh... my Freedom Flex card? and I see a charge that makes no sense. I need to report it.

AGENT: Okay, I can certainly help you with that. I'm looking at your account now, and I see the Chase Freedom Flex card ending in five nine nine seven. Is that the correct card?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that's the one. And there's a charge on there for three hundred ninety-two dollars and eighty-eight cents that I just do not recognize at all.

AGENT: Okay, three hundred ninety-two dollars and eighty-eight cents. Let me find that for you. And do you know the name of the merchant?

CUSTOMER: Well, that's the thing. At first I thought, you know, it might be Ross Dress for Less? My wife sometimes goes there and I let her use my card but she said she hasn't, and this amount just seems... way too high for a trip there anyway. It's usually just twenty bucks, thirty bucks. But that's what I guessed it was.

AGENT: I understand. One moment while I pull up the transaction details. We're looking for a charge from Ross Dress for Less... for $392.88... hmm. I'm not seeing a transaction from that merchant for that specific amount on the recent statement, sir.

CUSTOMER: No, wait. Hold on. I was just guessing. Let me pull up the actual statement on my computer, it was just loading. These websites, you know. So slow. Okay... here it is. It's loading... okay. Yeah, no. You're right. It's not Ross. It says... it says Pinecrest Outdoor Supply? What is that? I've never heard of that in my life.

AGENT: Pinecrest Outdoor Supply. Okay, I see it now. It posted two days ago.

CUSTOMER: Right, and I have no idea what it is. I'm in Atlanta, it's hot as anything, I am not buying outdoor supplies. It's not like I'm a professional mountain climber or anything. I work in an office. My big outdoor activity is walking to my car.

AGENT: I understand completely, Mr. Lindqvist. And thank you for clarifying the merchant name. So just to confirm, you did not authorize this charge from Pinecrest Outdoor Supply?

CUSTOMER: Not a chance. No.

AGENT: And is the physical card ending in five nine nine seven still in your possession?

CUSTOMER: Uh, yeah, let me check my wallet. It's right here. Yes, it's here.

AGENT: Okay, that's good. And have you attempted to contact the merchant, Pinecrest Outdoor Supply, to inquire about the charge?

CUSTOMER: No, I haven't, I don't even know who they are. I just saw the charge thirty minutes ago and called you. Should I have called them first?

AGENT: No, that's perfectly fine. It's a standard question we have to ask. Since you don't recognize the merchant or the transaction at all, we can proceed with opening a dispute. I'm going to need to ask you a few more formal questions for the record, okay?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, fine, whatever you need.

AGENT: Okay. I am now opening a formal dispute for the charge of $392.88 from the merchant listed as Pine Crest Outdoor Supply. Is that correct?

CUSTOMER: Pinecrest. One word. Pinecrest Outdoor Supply.

AGENT: My apologies. Thank you for the correction. Pinecrest Outdoor Supply. Okay, I've corrected it in the system. Now, Mr. Lindqvist, do you or any authorized users on your account recognize this transaction?

CUSTOMER: No, I'm the only user on the account and I do not recognize it.

AGENT: Did you receive any goods or services in relation to this charge?

CUSTOMER: No. Nothing.

AGENT: Has anyone had access to your card or card number recently that you know of?

CUSTOMER: Not that I know of. I mean, who knows with all the data breaches these days, but no, I haven't given it to anyone.

AGENT: Thank you for confirming all of that. It seems like a clear case of fraudulent activity. I am filing the dispute now on your behalf. This can take just a moment as the system processes it. How is the weather down in Atlanta today, by the way? You said it was hot.

CUSTOMER: Oh yeah. It's brutal. The humidity is the real killer, you know? Makes you not want to go outside at all, which is another reason I'm definitely not buying anything from an outdoor [inaudible] store.

AGENT: I can imagine. I'm up north and we're just finally getting some sun. Okay, it looks like the system has accepted the initial filing. I've created a dispute record for you. The reference number for the dispute is DSP-7530420.

CUSTOMER: Okay, hold on, let me get a pen. D... S... P... dash... seven five three zero... four two zero?

AGENT: That is correct. DSP-7530420. And I've also created a case for our call today, just for our internal records, and that number is CASE-4234533.

AGENT: CASE... four two three... four five three three.

AGENT: Perfect. Now, I want to explain the next steps so you know what to expect.

CUSTOMER: Okay. So do you take the charge off now?

AGENT: That's a great question. We have to follow a regulated process. We will issue a provisional credit for the full amount of three hundred ninety-two dollars and eighty-eight cents to your account. This credit is temporary while we investigate. It typically posts to your account within ten business days. Sometimes it's much faster, but that's the official timeline we provide.

CUSTOMER: Ten business days? So two weeks?

AGENT: Yes, sir. Ten business days, not including weekends or holidays. So about two weeks. You are not responsible for paying for that portion of your balance while it's under dispute. The provisional credit will cover it.

CUSTOMER: Okay... and what happens then?

AGENT: Once the provisional credit is posted, our back office team officially notifies the merchant and their bank of the dispute. The merchant then has a set amount of time to respond and provide evidence that the charge is valid—for instance, a receipt with your signature or proof of delivery to your address.

CUSTOMER: But they won't have that.

AGENT: If they don't have it, they typically won't respond, or they'll accept the dispute. In this case, the merchant has until July 7, 2026 to provide any compelling evidence.

CUSTOMER: July 7th, 2026? Wow, that's a long time.

AGENT: It is the maximum timeframe allowed by the network rules, yes. It's very rare for it to take that long. Most merchants who know a charge is invalid don't respond at all. If we receive no response by that deadline, or if the evidence they provide is not sufficient, the dispute is closed in your favor and the provisional credit we issued becomes permanent. We would send you a letter or email confirming this.

CUSTOMER: And what if they fight it? What if they somehow [crosstalk] make something up?

AGENT: It's very unlikely in a case like this where you don't recognize the merchant at all. If, in the very rare event they provide what appears to be valid evidence, we would contact you immediately with that evidence for you to review. But again, based on what you've told me, that is not the likely outcome here. The most important thing is that we've started the process, and you won't be out any money during the investigation.

CUSTOMER: Okay. Okay, I think I get it. So, I just wait for a credit to show up in the next two weeks.

AGENT: Exactly. And just to be safe, since we don't know how your card number was compromised, I would strongly recommend we close this card and issue you a new one. The new card would have a different number, and we can ship it to your Atlanta address in 3-5 business days. There's no charge for this.

CUSTOMER: Ah, jeez. That's a pain, all the autopay stuff I have to change. But I guess you're right. Okay, yes, let's do that.

AGENT: Okay, I am processing that request now. Your current card ending in five nine nine seven will be deactivated effective immediately, and a new card will be on its way to you. Is there a good callback number for you, Mr. Lindqvist, in case we get disconnected or need to reach you?

CUSTOMER: No, this is my mobile, it's the best one. You have it on file.

AGENT: Alright, perfect. So, to recap: We've filed dispute DSP-7530420 for the charge of $392.88. You should see a provisional credit for that amount within ten business days. We've closed the compromised card and a new one is being sent to you. Is there anything else at all I can help you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, that was it. Thank you for your help, Grace.

AGENT: You are very welcome, Mr. Lindqvist. Thank you for being a Chase customer and have a great rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye.

AGENT: Okay. I am now opening a formal dispute for the charge of $392.88 from the merchant listed as Pine Crest Outdoor Supply. Is that correct?

CUSTOMER: Pinecrest. One word. Pinecrest Outdoor Supply.

AGENT: My apologies. Thank you for the correction. Pinecrest Outdoor Supply. Okay, I've corrected it in the system. Now, Mr. Lindqvist, do you or any authorized users on your account recognize this transaction?

AGENT: Did you receive any goods or services in relation to this charge?

CUSTOMER: No. Nothing.

AGENT: Has anyone had access to your card or card number recently that you know of?

CUSTOMER: Not that I know of. I mean, who knows with all the data breaches these days, but no, I haven't given it to anyone.

AGENT: Thank you for confirming all of that. It seems like a clear case of fraudulent activity. I am filing the dispute now on your behalf. This can take just a moment as the system processes it. How is the weather down in Atlanta today, by the way? You said it was hot.

AGENT: I can imagine. I'm up north and we're just finally getting some sun. Okay, it looks like the system has accepted the initial filing. I've created a dispute record for you. The reference number for the dispute is DSP-7530420.

AGENT: That is correct. DSP-7530420. And I've also created a case for our call today, just for our internal records, and that number is CASE-4234533.

AGENT: Perfect. Now, I want to explain the next steps so you know what to expect.

CUSTOMER: But they won't have that.

AGENT: If they don't have it, they typically won't respond, or they'll accept the dispute. In this case, the merchant has until July 7, 2026 to provide any compelling evidence.

CUSTOMER: July 7th, 2026? Wow, that's a long time.

AGENT: It is the maximum timeframe allowed by the network rules, yes. It's very rare for it to take that long. Most merchants who know a charge is invalid don't respond at all. We would send you a letter or email confirming this.

CUSTOMER: And what if they fight it? What if they somehow [crosstalk] make something up?

AGENT: It's very unlikely in a case like this where you don't recognize the merchant at all. If, in the very rare event they provide what appears to be valid evidence, we would contact you immediately with that evidence for you to review. But again, based on what you've told me, that is not the likely outcome here. The most important thing is that we've started the process, and you won't be out any money during the investigation.

CUSTOMER: Okay. Okay, I think I get it. So, I just wait for a credit to show up in the next two weeks.

AGENT: Exactly. And just to be safe, since we don't know how your card number was compromised, I would strongly recommend we close this card and issue you a new one. The new card would have a different number, and we can ship it to your Atlanta address in 3-5 business days. There's no charge for this.

CUSTOMER: Ah, jeez. That's a pain, all the autopay stuff I have to change. But I guess you're right. Okay, yes, let's do that.

AGENT: Okay, I am processing that request now. Your current card ending in five nine nine seven will be deactivated effective immediately, and a new card will be on its way to you. Is there a good callback number for you, Mr. Lindqvist, in case we get disconnected or need to reach you?

CUSTOMER: No, this is my mobile, it's the best one. You have it on file.

AGENT: Alright, perfect. So, to recap: We've filed dispute DSP-7530420 for the charge of $392.88. You should see a provisional credit for that amount within ten business days. We've closed the compromised card and a new one is being sent to you. Is there anything else at all I can help you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, that was it. Thank you for your help, Grace.

AGENT: You are very welcome, Mr. Lindqvist. Thank you for being a Chase customer and have a great rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I got it.

AGENT: I've noted in the file that you are requesting a more detailed timeline for dispute `DSP-7530420` and an explanation of the next steps in the investigation process. Is that an accurate summary?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that's what I want.

AGENT: Perfect. I have submitted the request, and I can promise you that a supervisor will `call back` on that office line, `412-555-0147`, to discuss this with you. We will ensure that happens `by Friday`.

AGENT: They will review the entire case from the beginning, sir. While they have access to the same system I do, they can provide a deeper dive into the procedural aspects and set more specific expectations for you based on where we are in the process with the merchant's bank.

CUSTOMER: No, that's everything.

AGENT: Alright. Well, thank you again for calling Chase. I hope you have a good rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye.

cust_synth_009:C05.body:
Cx in branch, Marcus Lindqvist. Pulled him from the queue, he's a local guy from Atlanta. Pleasant, a little flustered but polite. Full CCK performed, ID verified against system, all good.

Primary issue is his card, the Chase Freedom Flex ending in *5997.
- Cx states the chip has stopped working consistently for about a week.
- First noticed it at the grocery store, had to swipe. Thought it was their machine.
- Then happened again at a gas station, and this morning at a coffee shop. Definitely the card, not the terminals. Per cx, the contactless tap feature also seems to be failing, but the magnetic stripe swipe is still working fine.
- He's worried b/c he has some travel coming up and doesn't want to be stuck somewhere with a card that only kind of works.

I took a look at the card. No visible damage, no cracks or obvious scratches on the chip, but that doesn't mean much. Sometimes they just fail internally. I tried cleaning it with a wipe just in case, but cx said he already tried that.

While I was pulling up the acct to order the replacement, we chatted a bit. I asked if everything else was okay with his banking. He laughed and said "as okay as it can be."
- He vaguely referenced the recent dispute he had open. Mentioned a charge from "that camping supply place" and said he was glad the credit came through. He's still waiting on the final letter about it. I saw the case notes on the overview screen so I knew what he was talking about. I just nodded and said the back office team is usually pretty thorough. He seemed to appreciate that. He mentioned he'd asked for a written summary and was told it would arrive within ten business days, so he's keeping an eye on the mail for that as well as the final dispute outcome.
- This seems to be the source of his travel anxiety. He and his partner, Jordan, are planning a hiking trip and he was worried about pre-paying for things w/ a card that had an open dispute, and now the chip issue on top of it. Assured him the two things are separate and a new card is a simple fix.

Walked cx through the card replacement process.
- Explained that for security, we issue a new card number. The new card will be a Chase Freedom Flex, just like his current one. All his account details, history, rewards, etc. will be automatically linked.
- Confirmed his mailing address on file. Read it back to him street, city, state, and zip. He confirmed it's correct.
- Confirmed his email. I read back marcus.lindqvist50@example.net. He chuckled and said "Yep, that's the one. With the dot. I always manage to mess that up when I'm typing it out for people." Reassured him it happens to everyone. Good to know the one on file is the one he's using.
- Explained the delivery options. Rush delivery comes w/ a fee (I think it's twenty bucks, didn't quote an exact price just said there's a fee). Standard mail is free and takes approx. 5-7 business days.
- Per cx, standard mail is fine. Since the mag stripe on *5997 still works for swipes and he can use it for online purchases, there's no huge emergency. He just wants the new card before his trip at the end of next month. Plenty of time.

I initiated the order in the system.

CARD REPLACEMENT ORDERED FOR ACCT ...XXXX.
REASON: DAMAGED/NON-FUNCTIONAL CHIP (CX REPORTED)
OLD CARD: *5997
NEW CARD ORDERED: *1073
DELIVERY METHOD: STANDARD MAIL (5-7 BUSINESS DAYS) TO ADDRESS ON FILE.
CARD *5997 REMAINS ACTIVE UNTIL NEW CARD *1073 IS ACTIVATED BY CX.

- Verbally confirmed with cx that the new card, ending in *1073, is on its way.
- Re-iterated that he needs to keep his current card (*5997) for now. It will continue to work for swipes and any recurring payments he has set up. Once the new card arrives, he'll need to call the number on the sticker to activate it. The moment he activates *1073, the old card *5997 will be permanently deactivated.
- Advised him to destroy the old card once the new one is up and running.
- Also reminded him to update his card number with any merchants that have it saved for automatic billing (utilities, subscriptions, etc.) after he activates the new one. He said he has a couple and made a note on his phone.

Cx seemed relieved. Asked if there was anything else I could help with. He paused and then asked if I could check the callback number on his profile. Said he'd given it to someone on the phone a while back and wanted to make sure it was his office line. I confirmed the number on file is 412-555-0147. He said "Perfect, that's the one. Sometimes I transpose the last two digits." Told him we all do. He said he's not always at that desk but it's the best place for messages if we ever need to follow up on anything.

Wrapped up the visit. Shook hands. He thanked me for making it easy. Overall a straightforward interaction, cx was easy to work with.

Follow-up:
- No f/u required from branch at this time. System will handle card mailing.
- Cx to receive and activate replacement card *1073 in 5-7 business days.
- If cx calls back about the card not arriving after that timeframe, check tracking. Otherwise, case closed on branch end.

cust_synth_009:C11.body:
Customer Marcus Lindqvist came into the branch today, was a walk-in, I was free so I took him at my desk. Seemed a little anxious but was very pleasant. He needed to get a cashier's check. He had all the information ready which is always a relief, had the payee name and amount written down on a piece of paper. I pulled up his profile and authenticated him.

CUST AUTHENTICATED VIA PIN PAD AND GOV ISSUED ID (GA DL).

We chatted a bit while the system was loading, you know how it is on a Monday afternoon. He lives in Atlanta, mentioned the traffic was lighter than he expected. He was asking about a cashier's check, so I confirmed the funds were available in his checking and the amount. He said he was making a large purchase from a private seller and they wouldn't take a personal check, which is pretty standard. I asked what he was buying, just making conversation, and he was a little cagey about it, just said it was for a "serious hobby." Fine by me. I confirmed the payee name and spelling with him twice to make sure we got it exactly right before printing the check.

While I was processing the debit from his account and getting the check request queued up in the system, he suddenly switched topics. He leaned forward a bit and said he had a kind of "what if" question. He wanted to know what the process would be if he ever wanted to close his accounts with us. He immediately followed it up by saying, very clearly, "I am NOT closing the account, I just want to know what the steps would be." He said it twice, actually. Stressed that he was happy with the bank, just curious about the logistics.

Of course, that's always a bit of a flag, so I tried to gently probe. I asked if he was planning on moving or if something had happened that we could help with. He laughed and said, "No, no, nothing like that. I'm not, like, moving to Antarctica or anything." He said he's just trying to get his financial life more organized and understand all the "ins and outs" of the products he has. He even mentioned that he was really pleased with how we handled a recent dispute he had. He said the company, Pinecrest Outdoor Supply, never responded and he was glad he got the credit back permanently without a big fight. So that was good to hear, a positive data point.

Since he brought up being happy with the service, I took the opportunity to mention the new cardmember offer, the one with the 75,000 bonus points, just in case he was thinking of consolidating his spending with us. He wasn't really interested, just sort of nodded and said "that's a lot of points." He seemed more focused on the account closure question. So I walked him through the general process: making sure any automatic payments or direct deposits are rerouted first, waiting for any pending transactions on his debit or credit card to clear fully, and then he could either come into a branch, call the main line, or send us a secure message online to make the formal request. I told him we'd obviously hate to see him go, especially since he's been with us for a while and uses his Freedom Flex card regularly.

He seemed satisfied with that answer. He said, "Okay, that's good to know. It's just good to know the process." Then he went right back to the cashier's check. He asked if it was ready yet. The timing was perfect, actually, as the final confirmation screen had just popped up. I printed the check and the receipt for him.

While he was signing the logbook for the cashier's check, I did a quick profile review with him. I confirmed his callback number is still 412-555-0276, which he said was his work number and was correct. I also verified his email on file is lindqvist.m91@example.org, and he confirmed that was right, said he'd just updated it recently. He also mentioned he was glad he updated it because he had to cancel a trip and it made the communication easier. He was supposed to go to Vancouver, Canada but something came up. He seemed a little bummed about it but said he'd reschedule eventually.

He took the check, folded it carefully with the receipt, and put it in his jacket pocket. He thanked me for my time and for answering his "weird question." I told him it wasn't weird at all and that we're here to help with any questions he has. He seemed to leave in a much better mood than when he came in.

Follow-up:
No immediate action needed. Customer stated he is not planning on closing his account. However, given the direct question, I've made a note on his profile to monitor for potential relationship review in the next 6-12 months. Will keep an eye out for any major changes in his banking patterns (e.g., direct deposit stopping, balance transfers out, etc.). No need for a follow-up call at this time as he seemed satisfied and stressed he was just curious.

AGENT: Got it. Thank you so much for verifying that information, Mr. Lindqvist. I have your account open here now. So, you said you had a question about your rewards points?

CUSTOMER: Yeah. Yeah, I do. I was, um, I was in a branch, I don't know maybe, maybe it was late last month? And I was talking to one of the bankers there, getting a cashier's check, and we were just chatting about the account. And he mentioned, I think he mentioned something about a... a promotion for bonus points. Like, a lot of them. I think he said seventy-five thousand points? And I was just looking at my account online and I don't see anything like that, and my balance isn't... it just doesn't seem right. Or, what I expected anyway.

AGENT: I see. Okay, let me take a look at the notes on your account, sir. One moment... hmm. Okay. Yes, I do see a note here from a branch visit at the end of August. And the banker did make a note about discussing a promotional offer. Let me just pull up the details of that specific offer... one second here... right. Okay. So, that offer for seventy-five thousand bonus points, it looks like that is a... it's a new account acquisition bonus. So it's for new clients who open a specific new credit card account and then meet a certain spending requirement in the first three months.

CUSTOMER: Oh. So... it's not for an existing account? Not for me?

AGENT: I'm afraid not, sir, at least not that particular one. That's one of our main public offers to attract new customers. I do apologize if that wasn't clear when you spoke with the banker.

CUSTOMER: No, no it's... it's probably my fault. I mean, we were talking about a bunch of different things. I must have just gotten my wires crossed. Okay. Well. That's... a little disappointing, but okay. That makes sense.

AGENT: I completely understand. I can take a look to see if there are any other targeted offers or spending promotions attached to your specific account, sometimes we have quarterly bonuses for [crosstalk] different categories—

CUSTOMER: Actually, you know what, sorry, sorry to cut you off. While I have you, can you check something else for me? Totally different topic. I just... I can never remember when my statement is supposed to close. I feel like the date changes. Can you just tell me when the next one is?

AGENT: Of course, not a problem at all. Let me switch screens here... okay. Looking at your billing cycle... I'm showing that your next statement date is scheduled to close on the twenty-fifth of this month.

CUSTOMER: The twenty-fifth. Okay. Is that something that's set in stone? Or can I change my closing date? It would be easier for me if it was, like, at the very end of the month or the first.

AGENT: That is a great question. It is possible to request a change to your closing date. We can't always guarantee a specific day, like the 1st or the 31st exactly, because the cycles are grouped into weeks. But we can usually move it. For example we could shift you to a cycle that closes in the first week of the month instead of the fourth week. The only thing is that it can take one to two full billing cycles for the change to take effect, so your next statement would probably still close on the 25th and then the one after that would have the new date.

CUSTOMER: Hmm. One to two cycles. And it might not be the exact day.

AGENT: That's correct. It would be a date in the first week.

CUSTOMER: You know what, never mind. That's... that sounds like more trouble than it's worth right now. I was just curious. The twenty-fifth is fine, I can live with that. Thanks for looking it up.

AGENT: You're very welcome, Mr. Lindqvist. So, just to circle back, were there any other questions about the rewards points? You had mentioned your balance didn't seem right, aside from the promotional offer.

CUSTOMER: Oh, yeah. Thanks. So, okay, forget the big seventy-five thousand point thing, that's solved. But I was also just... I was looking at my activity from like, the last statement. And I remember making a... a pretty decent-sized purchase, some outdoor gear. And I'm pretty sure that was in a bonus category, and I just... the number of points I earned for that month, it just seems low. I feel like something's missing from the calculation, you know?

AGENT: I understand. Let me review your recent transactions, and we can see what's going on. Do you happen to remember the name of the merchant or the approximate date of that purchase?

CUSTOMER: Uh, yeah, it was for some camping stuff. It would have been... sometime in the summer? Maybe July? End of July, I think. It was for... I don't know, three or four hundred bucks. Something like that. It was an online store.

AGENT: Okay, I'm filtering your transactions for July now, just a moment while it loads... Okay, I'm seeing several charges here... Let me see... hmm. Ah. I think I know what might have happened here. I am seeing a charge from, uh, let's see... Pine Crest outer supply? It was for three hundred ninety-two dollars and some change. Does that sound right?

AGENT: Ohhhh. Right. The tent pole thing. Man, I completely forgot about that. So the charge was reversed.

AGENT: That's correct, yes. I see that charge, but then I also see a full credit posted back to your account just a few days later for that exact same amount. The notes indicate it was related to a dispute, uh, DSP-7530420, which was resolved in your favor.

CUSTOMER: Yeah. Yeah, okay. The company sent the wrong item and then just went dark, so I had to dispute it. I totally forgot that's when it was. Wow. Okay.

AGENT: Right, and so what happens is, when you make the purchase, the points are often shown as 'pending'. But if the charge is refunded or credited back to the account for any reason, like a return or a successful dispute, the pending points associated with that purchase are also reversed. So you wouldn't have earned points on that three hundred ninety-two dollars since you ultimately received a full refund.

CUSTOMER: That makes perfect, perfect sense. That's exactly the amount I couldn't account for. I was looking at my list of purchases and just completely glossed over the fact that that one was, you know, taken off the bill. Okay. Well, I feel a little stupid now, but thank you for figuring that out.

AGENT: Not at all, sir, please don't feel that way. It's an extremely common question, and it's very easy to lose track of which credits have posted, especially when you're not expecting them. I'm just glad we were able to get to the bottom of it for you. It's better to call and ask than to wonder what's going on with your account.

CUSTOMER: Yeah, you're right. I was also... thinking about a trip I was going to take, to Vancouver, and I had a travel notice on the card but I ended up canceling the trip, and I was worried maybe that messed something up with the points categories but [inaudible] that dispute thing explains it all.

AGENT: I see the note about the cancelled travel notice as well, but no, that wouldn't have had any impact on your points earned. It was definitely the reversal of that charge from the dispute.

CUSTOMER: Cool. Well, you've been a huge help Rafael. Answered all my questions.

AGENT: It was my pleasure, Mr. Lindqvist. Was there anything else at all I could assist you with today? Any other questions about your card or your account?

CUSTOMER: Nope, that's everything. I'm all set.

AGENT: Wonderful. In that case, just for your records, I've documented our conversation and the questions we discussed under case number CASE-3420358. Thank you for calling Chase today, and please have a wonderful rest of your afternoon.

CUSTOMER: You too, thanks again. Bye now.

AGENT: Goodbye.

CUSTOMER: The twenty-fifth. Okay. Is that something that's set in stone? Or can I change my closing date? It would be easier for me if it was, like, at the very end of the month or the first.

AGENT: That is a great question. It is possible to request a change to your closing date. We can't always guarantee a specific day, like the 1st or the 31st exactly, because the cycles are grouped into weeks. But we can usually move it. For example we could shift you to a cycle that closes in the first week of the month instead of the fourth week. The only thing is that it can take one to two full billing cycles for the change to take effect, so your next statement would probably still close on the 25th and then the one after that would have the new date.

CUSTOMER: Hmm. One to two cycles. And it might not be the exact day.

AGENT: That's correct. It would be a date in the first week.

CUSTOMER: You know what, never mind. That's... that sounds like more trouble than it's worth right now. I was just curious. The twenty-fifth is fine, I can live with that. Thanks for looking it up.

AGENT: You're very welcome, Mr. Lindqvist. So, just to circle back, were there any other questions about the rewards points? You had mentioned your balance didn't seem right, aside from the promotional offer.

CUSTOMER: Oh, yeah. Thanks. So, okay, forget the big seventy-five thousand point thing, that's solved. But I was also just... I was looking at my activity from like, the last statement. And I remember making a... a pretty decent-sized purchase, some outdoor gear. And I'm pretty sure that was in a bonus category, and I just... the number of points I earned for that month, it just seems low. I feel like something's missing from the calculation, you know?

AGENT: I understand. Let me review your recent transactions, and we can see what's going on. Do you happen to remember the name of the merchant or the approximate date of that purchase?

CUSTOMER: Uh, yeah, it was for some camping stuff. It would have been... sometime in the summer? Maybe July? End of July, I think. It was for... I don't know, three or four hundred bucks. Something like that. It was an online store.

AGENT: Okay, I'm filtering your transactions for July now, just a moment while it loads... Okay, I'm seeing several charges here... Let me see... hmm. Ah. I think I know what might have happened here. I am seeing a charge from, uh, let's see... Pine Crest outer supply? It was for three hundred ninety-two dollars and some change. Does that sound right?

AGENT: Ohhhh. Right. The tent pole thing. Man, I completely forgot about that. So the charge was reversed.

AGENT: That's correct, yes. I see that charge, but then I also see a full credit posted back to your account just a few days later for that exact same amount. The notes indicate it was related to a dispute, uh, DSP-7530420, which was resolved in your favor.

CUSTOMER: Yeah. Yeah, okay. The company sent the wrong item and then just went dark, so I had to dispute it. I totally forgot that's when it was. Wow. Okay.

AGENT: Right, and so what happens is, when you make the purchase, the points are often shown as 'pending'. But if the charge is refunded or credited back to the account for any reason, like a return or a successful dispute, the pending points associated with that purchase are also reversed. So you wouldn't have earned points on that three hundred ninety-two dollars since you ultimately received a full refund.

CUSTOMER: That makes perfect, perfect sense. That's exactly the amount I couldn't account for. I was looking at my list of purchases and just completely glossed over the fact that that one was, you know, taken off the bill. Okay. Well, I feel a little stupid now, but thank you for figuring that out.

AGENT: Not at all, sir, please don't feel that way. It's an extremely common question, and it's very easy to lose track of which credits have posted, especially when you're not expecting them. I'm just glad we were able to get to the bottom of it for you. It's better to call and ask than to wonder what's going on with your account.

CUSTOMER: Yeah, you're right. I was also... thinking about a trip I was going to take, to Vancouver, and I had a travel notice on the card but I ended up canceling the trip, and I was worried maybe that messed something up with the points categories but [inaudible] that dispute thing explains it all.

AGENT: I see the note about the cancelled travel notice as well, but no, that wouldn't have had any impact on your points earned. It was definitely the reversal of that charge from the dispute.

CUSTOMER: Cool. Well, you've been a huge help Rafael. Answered all my questions.

AGENT: It was my pleasure, Mr. Lindqvist. Was there anything else at all I could assist you with today? Any other questions about your card or your account?

CUSTOMER: Nope, that's everything. I'm all set.

AGENT: Wonderful. In that case, just for your records, I've documented our conversation and the questions we discussed under case number CASE-3420358. Thank you for calling Chase today, and please have a wonderful rest of your afternoon.

CUSTOMER: You too, thanks again. Bye now.

AGENT: Goodbye.

CUSTOMER: Hi Grace, yes, hello. My name is Sofia Doyle. I'm calling about a charge on my statement that I don't think is mine. It's... it's a pretty big one.

AGENT: Okay Ms. Doyle, I can certainly help you with that. I just need to ask a few questions to verify your identity before we proceed. This is for your protection.

AGENT: Okay. And which charge is it that you're questioning?

AGENT: Okay, I'm looking at your recent transactions now for the card ending in two eight three seven. I see a charge for four hundred seventy-three dollars and thirty-one cents.

CUSTOMER: That's the one. Does it say Kohl's? Because I swear I didn't spend that much.

AGENT: One moment ma'am. Let me just expand the details here... hmm. The merchant name listed isn't Kohl's. It's...

AGENT: Not a problem at all, take your time.

AGENT: It's quite alright, Mr. Doyle, thank you. So, Ms. Doyle, just to be perfectly clear, you do not recognize this transaction from Golden Gate Luggage Co. for $473.31, and you're certain you didn't authorize it?

CUSTOMER: So is the charge taken off my account now?

The charge itself will remain on the account for now, but we will begin the process of issuing a provisional, or temporary, credit for the full amount. It will appear on your statement as a credit for the same amount, four hundred seventy-three dollars and thirty-one cents.

CUSTOMER: Ten business days? So I have to pay it in the meantime? My payment is due soon.

AGENT: You are not responsible for paying the disputed amount while it's under investigation. You should continue to make at least your minimum payment on the remaining, undisputed balance to keep your account in good standing. The provisional credit will cover the disputed charge once it posts.

CUSTOMER: Okay... okay, I think I understand. So I just pay the rest of my bill, but not that part.

AGENT: Exactly. Now, do you have a pen and paper handy? I need to give you two very important reference numbers.

CUSTOMER: Yes, hold on. Let me grab one... okay, I'm ready.

AGENT: Perfect. And the second number is the case number for our conversation today. That one is C-A-S-E, dash, five, seven, two, eight, four, one, nine.

CUSTOMER: Case... five seven two eight four one nine. Okay. So I have two numbers. DSP-1512689 and CASE-5728419.

AGENT: That is absolutely correct. Now, here's what happens next. Our disputes department will contact the merchant, Golden Gate Luggage and Co., to get their side of the story. CUSTOMER: And what if they can't? Or what if they just ignore you?

AGENT: An excellent question. The merchant has a set amount of time to respond to our inquiry. We require them to respond by a specific deadline. In this case, they have until July 2, 2026 to provide their evidence.

CUSTOMER: July? That's months away!

AGENT: Yes ma'am, the process does allow them a generous window to investigate on their end and reply. However, if they fail to respond by that date, July 2, 2026, or if the documentation they provide is not sufficient to prove the charge was authorized by you, the provisional credit we issued to your account will be made permanent. The dispute is closed in your favor, and you'll never have to worry about that charge again.

CUSTOMER: And what if they DO have proof? What if someone did steal my card and used it?

AGENT: If they provide compelling evidence, our team would review it and contact you with the next steps. But please don't worry about that for now. In many of these cases, it's simply a billing error, or the merchant is unable to validate the charge. We just have to follow the process.

CUSTOMER: Okay. Wow. It's a lot. So, just to recap... you've filed the dispute. I don't pay that four hundred seventy-three dollar amount. I'll get a temporary credit in about two weeks. And the luggage company has until July to prove it was me, and if they can't, it's all over.

AGENT: You've summarized it perfectly, Ms. Doyle. That is exactly right. Is there anything about the process that's unclear?

CUSTOMER: No, I think I've got it. It's just very frustrating you know. You try to be so careful and then [inaudible] happens.

AGENT: I completely understand. It's unsettling, and I'm very sorry you're having to go through this. We're going to do everything we can to get it resolved for you. Before we finish up, is there a good callback number I can note on the account in case the disputes team needs to reach you directly?

CUSTOMER: Oh, no that's okay. You have my email, right? The sofiad3 one? Just use that. I check that constantly. I'm not great with answering calls from numbers I don't know.

AGENT: Not a problem at all. I've confirmed your email is noted as the preferred contact method. Is there anything else at all I can assist you with today, Ms. Doyle? Any other questions about your account?

CUSTOMER: No, that was the big one. Thank you for your help, Grace. You've been very clear.

AGENT: You are most welcome. Thank you for being a Chase customer, and I hope you have a much better rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye now.

AGENT: Goodbye.

cust_synth_016:C05.body:
Cx Sofia Doyle in branch approx. 2:15 PM. Was a walk-in. Seemed a bit stressed but was very polite.
Primary issue is w/ her physical card.

- Cx presented her Chase Slate Edge card (*2837) for inspection.
- Card is in very poor shape. The top right corner is completely snapped off, and the magnetic stripe is visibly scratched and worn down. Cx says she's had it for a long time.
- Per cx, she has been having intermittent issues with it for weeks, where she has to swipe it multiple times at a terminal.
- Today, the swipe function failed entirely at a local business. She said the chip still works, so she was able to complete that purchase, but she is concerned the whole card will just stop working soon. She is traveling from her home in Charlotte and doesn't want to be left without a usable card.

Pulled up cx acct to begin.
Verified cx identity using her NC driver's license. Photo and info match what we have on file. Completed CCK verification questions, all answers correct.
Noted the address in Charlotte and asked about her visit. She's here for another week visiting her sister.
Before processing the card request, I performed a quick relationship review, noting the recent contacts on the acct.
I mentioned to her, "Looks like we've been in touch a couple of times recently, I just want to make sure all your other concerns have been taken care of."
Cx acknowledged this. She brought up the fraud dispute from back in March. Mentioned the "weird charge from that luggage place" and said what a headache it was. She confirmed that she did see the provisional credit post to her acct, which she was very happy about. Seems satisfied with how that was handled.
I also saw the recent email correspondence note. I asked if she had received the paper statement she requested last month.
She confirmed she did receive it. Stated, "Oh yes, thank you. My wife, Renata, and I find it much easier to have the physical copies for our records. We're a bit old-fashioned that way." This aligns with notes from a prior call.
I also wanted to proactively confirm her contact info. I saw the note about the email change. I read the email on file, sofia.doyle73@example.net, back to her to ensure it was correct.
Cx confirmed it. "Yes, that's it. I'm so glad that agent I chatted with double-checked. I'm terrible at typing and almost gave them the wrong one."
Finally, I confirmed the callback number on file (608-555-0481). She said yes, that's her office landline and it's the most reliable way to reach her if needed, as her cell service can be spotty.

Moved on to resolving the card issue.
Advised cx that given the physical damage, the best course of action is to order a replacement.
I explained the options. We can order a new card via standard mail, or we can expedite it for a fee.
Cx asked how long standard mail would take. Advised approx. 5-7 business days.
She declined the expedited shipping, stating that since the chip on her current card (*2837) still works, she is okay to wait for the standard delivery to her home address.
She asked a key question: will ordering a new card deactivate her current one?
I assured her that the current card, *2837, will remain fully active and usable until she receives the new replacement card in the mail and calls to activate it. This seemed to be her main concern.
I proceeded with the replacement card order in the system.
Selected reason code for DAMAGED/WORN card.
Confirmed her mailing address in Charlotte is correct for the delivery.
Submitted the order. I've pasted the system confirmation note below for the record.
---
CARD SERVICES SYSTEM NOTIFICATION:
ACCT: ...-XXXX
CARD REPLACEMENT ORDER SUBMITTED 20-MAY-2026 14:28 EST
REASON: CUST REQ - CARD DAMAGED/WORN
EXISTING CARD: *2837
NEW CARD ORDERED: *6065
DELIVERY METHOD: STANDARD US MAIL (5-7 BUSINESS DAYS)
DELIVERY ADDR: ON FILE
BRANCH ID: 0744 OPR: OMAR_A
---
I read the confirmation back to the cx, verbally confirming that her new card, ending in *6065, is on its way to her home and should arrive within a week or so. She was pleased.

While waiting for the system receipt to print, I made some additional conversation to see if there were other needs. Offered her a bottle of water, which she took.
She then asked a hypothetical question. "While I have you here, and I don't plan on this happening, but what are the late fees on this account? I was just reviewing our budget with my wife and we were curious."
I pulled up the standard fee disclosure for her product to ensure I provided accurate, generic information. I read from the document, "For this card, as per the standard terms, if a payment is ever late, the fee can be up to $41.00. The specific amount can vary based on the account balance and prior payment history, but that's the maximum." I stressed this was general info and not related to her acct status. She said that was helpful.
No other needs or sales opportunities were identified. Cx was focused on her one issue.
I printed the interaction receipt for her, summarized the plan one last time (new card *6065 on its way, old card *2837 works until then), and walked her to the exit.

Follow-up:
- No immediate f/u needed on my part. The card order is in the system.
- Cx left satisfied with the solution.
- May check acct in 7-10 days to confirm activation of new card *6065 as a courtesy.
- No products offered, no sales leads generated. Purely a service interaction.
