- Card is in very poor shape. The top right corner is completely snapped off, and the magnetic stripe is visibly scratched and worn down. Cx says she's had it for a long time.
- Per cx, she has been having intermittent issues with it for weeks, where she has to swipe it multiple times at a terminal.
- Today, the swipe function failed entirely at a local business. She said the chip still works, so she was able to complete that purchase, but she is concerned the whole card will just stop working soon. She is traveling from her home in Charlotte and doesn't want to be left without a usable card.

Pulled up cx acct to begin.
Verified cx identity using her NC driver's license. Photo and info match what we have on file. Completed CCK verification questions, all answers correct.
Noted the address in Charlotte and asked about her visit. She's here for another week visiting her sister.
Before processing the card request, I performed a quick relationship review, noting the recent contacts on the acct.
I mentioned to her, "Looks like we've been in touch a couple of times recently, I just want to make sure all your other concerns have been taken care of."
Cx acknowledged this. She brought up the fraud dispute from back in March. Mentioned the "weird charge from that luggage place" and said what a headache it was. She confirmed that she did see the provisional credit post to her acct, which she was very happy about. Seems satisfied with how that was handled.
I also saw the recent email correspondence note. I asked if she had received the paper statement she requested last month.
She confirmed she did receive it. Stated, "Oh yes, thank you. My wife, Renata, and I find it much easier to have the physical copies for our records. We're a bit old-fashioned that way." This aligns with notes from a prior call.
I also wanted to proactively confirm her contact info. I saw the note about the email change. I read the email on file, sofia.doyle73@example.net, back to her to ensure it was correct.
Cx confirmed it. "Yes, that's it. I'm so glad that agent I chatted with double-checked. I'm terrible at typing and almost gave them the wrong one."
Finally, I confirmed the callback number on file (608-555-0481). She said yes, that's her office landline and it's the most reliable way to reach her if needed, as her cell service can be spotty.

Moved on to resolving the card issue.
Advised cx that given the physical damage, the best course of action is to order a replacement.
I explained the options. We can order a new card via standard mail, or we can expedite it for a fee.
Cx asked how long standard mail would take. Advised approx. 5-7 business days.
She declined the expedited shipping, stating that since the chip on her current card (*2837) still works, she is okay to wait for the standard delivery to her home address.
She asked a key question: will ordering a new card deactivate her current one?
I assured her that the current card, *2837, will remain fully active and usable until she receives the new replacement card in the mail and calls to activate it. This seemed to be her main concern.
I proceeded with the replacement card order in the system.
Selected reason code for DAMAGED/WORN card.
Confirmed her mailing address in Charlotte is correct for the delivery.
Submitted the order. I've pasted the system confirmation note below for the record.
---
CARD SERVICES SYSTEM NOTIFICATION:
ACCT: ...-XXXX
CARD REPLACEMENT ORDER SUBMITTED 20-MAY-2026 14:28 EST
REASON: CUST REQ - CARD DAMAGED/WORN
EXISTING CARD: *2837
NEW CARD ORDERED: *6065
DELIVERY METHOD: STANDARD US MAIL (5-7 BUSINESS DAYS)
DELIVERY ADDR: ON FILE
BRANCH ID: 0744 OPR: OMAR_A
---
I read the confirmation back to the cx, verbally confirming that her new card, ending in *6065, is on its way to her home and should arrive within a week or so. She was pleased.

While waiting for the system receipt to print, I made some additional conversation to see if there were other needs. Offered her a bottle of water, which she took.
She then asked a hypothetical question. "While I have you here, and I don't plan on this happening, but what are the late fees on this account? I was just reviewing our budget with my wife and we were curious."
I pulled up the standard fee disclosure for her product to ensure I provided accurate, generic information. I read from the document, "For this card, as per the standard terms, if a payment is ever late, the fee can be up to $41.00. The specific amount can vary based on the account balance and prior payment history, but that's the maximum." I stressed this was general info and not related to her acct status. She said that was helpful.
No other needs or sales opportunities were identified. Cx was focused on her one issue.
I printed the interaction receipt for her, summarized the plan one last time (new card *6065 on its way, old card *2837 works until then), and walked her to the exit.

Follow-up:
- No immediate f/u needed on my part. The card order is in the system.
- Cx left satisfied with the solution.
- May check acct in 7-10 days to confirm activation of new card *6065 as a courtesy.
- No products offered, no sales leads generated. Purely a service interaction.

AGENT: It was my pleasure, Ms. Doyle. I’m just glad we could get it resolved for you quickly. I will go ahead and close out this case, CASE-1453067, as resolved.

CUSTOMER: Fantastic.

AGENT: Well, thank you for being a Chase customer, and I hope you and your wife have a wonderful trip to Brazil if you do decide to go.

CUSTOMER: Thank you! You have a great rest of your day.

AGENT: You too. Goodbye.

CUSTOMER: Bye-bye.

cust_synth_016:C11.body:
Customer Sofia Doyle (resides in Charlotte, NC) came into the branch today around 2:30 PM. Seemed a little stressed but was very pleasant. I pulled up her profile after completing standard KYC verification with her driver's license. She said she had a few different things to discuss.

Her first question was about getting a cashier's check. She's moving to a new apartment locally and needs it for the security deposit and first month's rent. We talked for a minute about the Charlotte rental market, she said it's been a real challenge finding a place and she's just glad it's over. I confirmed she had sufficient funds in her checking account to cover the check.

As I was getting ready to process the request, she held up her hand and said, "Actually, can we pause on that for one second? I have another question that's been on my mind." She then brought up a recent dispute she had filed. She couldn't remember the exact details but mentioned it was about some luggage that was never delivered. I saw the closed case in her history and was able to confirm it was resolved in her favor. She was very happy about that, said "Oh good, I just wanted to make sure that was permanent. That $473.31 was a lot to lose, and you guys handled it really well, so thank you." I told her she was welcome and that we were glad it worked out.

This seemed to lead into her next train of thought, which was more forward-looking. She got a little quiet and then asked about the process for closing an account. She was very quick to clarify, saying, and I am quoting this directly because she was very emphatic: "I am NOT closing the account, I just want to know what the steps would be." She explained that with her move, she's been trying to "get her financial house in order" and was just curious what the process looked like, in case she ever decided to consolidate her banking relationships in the future.

I explained that it's a straightforward process. We'd need to ensure the account has a zero balance, with no pending transactions or automatic payments scheduled. Any direct deposits would need to be rerouted first. Once clear, she could close it either in a branch or by sending a written request. I took this as an opportunity for a soft retention effort. I mentioned that we value her as a customer and would be sorry to see her go, even hypothetically. I also told her about a targeted promotion we have running right now for a $200.00 statement credit on her Chase Slate Edge card if she hits a certain spend threshold over the next quarter. She seemed interested but didn't commit, just said "Oh, that's good to know, thank you."

Then she pivoted back to her original request. "Okay, thank you for explaining all that. Very helpful. Now, about that cashier's check..." I re-confirmed the payee name (the property management company) and the total amount. She needed the check before the end of the day as the lease signing is tomorrow morning. She mentioned that the landlord needs the security deposit cleared by the end of next month, but she wanted to get it all done at once. I processed the check request, printed it, and had my manager provide the second signature. While we waited, I double-checked her contact information on file to make sure it was current after her move. I confirmed her email is doyle.s99@example.org and her best callback number is 608-555-0779, which she said was correct. She mentioned the number was new-ish, her work line, and was glad we had it right.

Handed her the check and the receipt. She had one last question about her card, the Chase Slate Edge (*6065). She mentioned a trip to Iceland that she had to postpone a few weeks ago and wanted to know what the foreign transaction fees would be if she rebooked it for next year. I confirmed her card has no foreign transaction fees, which she was very pleased to hear. She said that makes it easier to just use the one card when she travels. I also reminded her that if she does submit a payment for something like a deposit on a future trip, and it doesn't arrive, the funds should be returned to her account within ten business days, but to call us if they aren't. She thanked me for my time and said I was very helpful. Overall a very positive interaction, despite the slightly alarming question about account closure. I do not believe she is a high risk for attrition at this time; seems more like she was doing general life admin.

Follow-up:
- Set reminder to check in with customer in mid-October via email. Frame it as a courtesy follow-up to see if she's settled into her new place. Can also gently re-mention the credit card spend offer at that time.

cust_synth_033:C01.body:
IVR: Thank you for calling Card Services. Your call may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance. To continue in English, press one. Para Español, oprima dos. Please have your card number ready. If you are calling about a lost or stolen card, press one. For questions about your balance, payments, or recent transactions, press two. To activate a new card, press three. For all other inquiries, press four or stay on the line and an agent will be with you shortly.

[BEEP]

IVR: Please say or enter the last four digits of your card number.

CUSTOMER: Representative.

IVR: I'm sorry, I didn't get that. To hear your account balance, say "balance." For recent transactions, say "transactions." To speak with a customer service representative, say "representative."

CUSTOMER: Representative!

IVR: Okay, connecting you to the next available agent.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can manage your account, check your balance, and make payments online at our website or through our mobile app? Ask your representative for details. And for a limited time, when you're approved for our new Voyager Rewards card, you can earn a $200.00 statement credit after you spend one thousand dollars in the first three months. Don't miss out on this exclusive offer. Thank you for your patience. An agent will be with you as soon as possible.

AGENT: Thank you for calling Card Services, this is David speaking. To get started can I have your full name please?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it’s Ingrid Okafor.

AGENT: Okay Ms. Okafor, thank you. And just to verify the account, can you tell me the city you live in?

CUSTOMER: San Diego.

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. I have your account pulled up here. How can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, I’m looking at my most recent statement, the one that just closed a few days ago, and there’s a charge on there I really don’t think is mine.

AGENT: Okay, I can certainly look into that for you. Which card is this on?

CUSTOMER: It’s the Amazon Prime Visa, the one ending in… uh… 6824.

AGENT: Got it, the Amazon Prime card. And what is the amount of the charge you're concerned about?

CUSTOMER: It’s for two hundred seventeen dollars and seventy-six cents.

AGENT: Okay, two hundred seventeen and seventy-six. And do you know the name of the merchant?

CUSTOMER: Well that’s the thing, I’m not sure. I saw the amount and I thought, oh, maybe that was when I went to Ross Dress for Less and bought a bunch of stuff for the house, but it seems high for that and I usually remember a trip like that. I just… I don't recognize it.

AGENT: I understand. It can be confusing when the merchant name on the statement doesn't match the store. Let me see what I can find. Okay, I see a charge for that amount posted about two weeks ago. For this type of inquiry, I’ll need to transfer you over to our disputes department. They have the specialized tools to handle unrecognized charges. Is that alright?

CUSTOMER: Oh. Yes, okay, that's fine. Will I have to wait on hold again for a long time?

AGENT: It should be just a moment, I'll do a warm transfer for you so you don't have to explain everything again. Please hold.

[CLICK]

HOLD MESSAGE: Thank you for holding. Your satisfaction is important to us. An agent will be right with you. Did you know you can earn a $200.00 statement credit when you're approved for our new Voyager Rewards card? Ask your representative for more details on how to apply today.

AGENT: Hi, thank you for holding, my name is Grace. I see you're calling about an unrecognized charge on your Amazon Prime Visa from a clothing store?

CUSTOMER: Oh um no, not exactly. The first guy must have misunderstood me. I thought at first it was a clothing store, I thought maybe it was Ross Dress for Less, but then I looked at the statement online while I was on hold and it's something else entirely. It's not a clothing store.

AGENT: Oh, okay, I apologize for that. I'm happy to get that corrected for you. Can you tell me what merchant name you're seeing on the statement?

CUSTOMER: Yes. It says Summit Ridge Ski Rentals. And I have never, ever been there. I don't even ski. My husband and I went to the mountains once, like, ten years ago, but we live in San Diego. We go to the beach, we don’t ski.

AGENT: I see. Summit Ridge Ski Rentals. I’m just noting that down. And can you confirm the amount for me one more time?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it was for **two hundred seventeen dollars and seventy-six cents**.

AGENT: Okay, I have it here. I'm looking at the transaction now. It posted on February 20th. Now, Ms. Okafor, I have to ask a few standard questions for the dispute process, is that okay?

CUSTOMER: Yes, of course.

AGENT: First, is the physical card ending in 6824 in your possession right now?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it’s in my wallet right here.

AGENT: Okay. And have you lent the card to anyone, a family member or friend, who might have used it?

CUSTOMER: No. No one else uses my cards.

AGENT: And have you tried contacting the merchant, Summit Bridge Ski Rentals, to ask them about the charge?

CUSTOMER: Summit *Ridge*. And no, I haven't. I just saw it on the statement maybe an hour ago and called you first. I wouldn't even know who to call there.

AGENT: That’s perfectly fine, you don’t have to. It's just a question we're required to ask. So just to be perfectly clear, you did not authorize this transaction, and you did not receive any goods or services from this merchant.

CUSTOMER: That is one hundred percent correct.

AGENT: Okay. Thank you for confirming that. Actually, while I have you, this is totally unrelated, but does this card have any kind of travel insurance? My husband was just saying we should book our summer vacation and I was wondering if I should use this card for the flights.

CUSTOMER: That's a great question. Let me just pull up the benefits guide for your specific card... yes, it looks like your Amazon Prime Visa does come with some travel and emergency assistance services, and a baggage delay insurance. For full trip cancellation or interruption insurance, that's usually a feature on our premium travel cards, but this one does offer some good protections.

AGENT: Okay, right.

CUSTOMER: You can view the full guide to benefits by logging into your account online, it'll have all the specifics for you there. It's a PDF document.

AGENT: Oh okay, I can find that. Thank you. Sorry to get off track. So, back to this ski rental place. What happens now? Do you just take the charge off?

CUSTOMER: I wish it were that simple, but there's a process we have to follow. What I'm doing now is officially opening a billing dispute. This creates a formal investigation into the charge. So, I'm submitting this on your behalf right now. Okay, that's submitted. I have a dispute reference number for you. It's D... S... P... as in Paul... dash... 5... 9... 7... 6... 1... 4... 7.

CUSTOMER: Okay hold on, let me get a pen. [inaudible] Okay, sorry. Can you give me that again?

AGENT: Of course. It’s dispute number DSP-5976147.

CUSTOMER: D... S... P... 5976147. Got it.

AGENT: And I'm also creating a case number for our conversation today, just for your records. That number is CASE-1603624.

CUSTOMER: CASE-1603624. Okay. So... what does that mean, a dispute? Do I still have to pay this? My payment is due in a couple of weeks.

AGENT: Great question. What will happen next is we will issue a provisional, or temporary, credit to your account for the full amount of the disputed charge, for the two hundred seventeen dollars and seventy-six cents. This credit is not a permanent resolution, it's just so you don't have to pay for the charge while we investigate.

CUSTOMER: Oh, thank you. When will I see that credit?

AGENT: It typically posts to your account within ten business days, sometimes much sooner, maybe two or three days. You'll see it appear as a credit with a note that it's related to a dispute.

CUSTOMER: Okay, ten business days. So that should be before the payment is due. That's good.

AGENT: Yes, it should. And from there, we will contact the merchant's bank and provide them with the details of your claim. They then have a set amount of time to respond with there evidence. [crosstalk] Sorry, go ahead.

CUSTOMER: [crosstalk] So they have to prove I was there?

AGENT: Exactly. They would need to provide evidence that the charge is legitimate, like a signed receipt or an equipment rental agreement with your information on it. The merchant, Summit Ridge Ski Rentals, has until **July 4, 2026**, to respond to our request.

CUSTOMER: Wow, that’s a long time from now. July fourth?

AGENT: It is, yes. The regulations allow them a certain number of days, and it can take a while. But don't worry, the provisional credit will stay on your account during that whole time. If they fail to respond by **July 4, 2026**, or if they respond but can't provide sufficient proof, the dispute is closed in your favor, and that provisional credit automatically becomes permanent.

CUSTOMER: And what if they do have something? Like what if someone stole my number and forged my signature?

AGENT: If they provide evidence, we review it carefully. If it appears to be fraudulent, we would continue to fight the charge on your behalf. If they provide convincing evidence that the charge is valid, we would notify you and, unfortunately, the credit would be reversed. But in cases like this, where you've never been to the merchant, it's very, very rare for that to happen. The most likely outcome is that the merchant either won't respond or they'll accept the chargeback.

CUSTOMER: Okay. That makes sense. It's just so strange. I've never had this happen before. It makes you feel a little... violated, you know?

AGENT: I completely understand. It's an unsettling feeling. We’ll do everything we can to get this resolved for you. Just to confirm, I've filed dispute DSP-5976147 for the charge of $217.76 from Summit Ridge Ski Rentals. We've issued no permanent credit yet but a provisional credit will post within ten business days, and the merchant has until July 4th of this year to respond. Does that all sound correct?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s all correct. Thank you, Grace, you've been very helpful.

AGENT: You are most welcome, Ms. Okafor. Is there anything else at all I can assist you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, that was it. Thank you again.

AGENT: It was my pleasure. Thank you for being a customer, and have a wonderful rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye bye.

AGENT: That’s perfectly fine, you don’t have to. It's just a question we're required to ask. So just to be perfectly clear, you did not authorize this transaction, and you did not receive any goods or services from this merchant.

CUSTOMER: That is one hundred percent correct.

AGENT: Okay. Thank you for confirming that. Actually, while I have you, this is totally unrelated, but does this card have any kind of travel insurance? My husband was just saying we should book our summer vacation and I was wondering if I should use this card for the flights.

CUSTOMER: That's a great question. Let me just pull up the benefits guide for your specific card... yes, it looks like your Amazon Prime Visa does come with some travel and emergency assistance services, and a baggage delay insurance. For full trip cancellation or interruption insurance, that's usually a feature on our premium travel cards, but this one does offer some good protections.

AGENT: Okay, right.

CUSTOMER: You can view the full guide to benefits by logging into your account online, it'll have all the specifics for you there. It's a PDF document.

AGENT: Oh okay, I can find that. Thank you. Sorry to get off track. So, back to this ski rental place. What happens now? Do you just take the charge off?

CUSTOMER: I wish it were that simple, but there's a process we have to follow. What I'm doing now is officially opening a billing dispute. This creates a formal investigation into the charge. So, I'm submitting this on your behalf right now. Okay, that's submitted. I have a dispute reference number for you. It's D... S... P... as in Paul... dash... 5... 9... 7... 6... 1... 4... 7.

CUSTOMER: Okay hold on, let me get a pen. [inaudible] Okay, sorry. Can you give me that again?

AGENT: Of course. It’s dispute number DSP-5976147.

CUSTOMER: D... S... P... 5976147. Got it.

AGENT: And I'm also creating a case number for our conversation today, just for your records. That number is CASE-1603624.

CUSTOMER: CASE-1603624. Okay. So... what does that mean, a dispute? Do I still have to pay this? My payment is due in a couple of weeks.

AGENT: Great question. What will happen next is we will issue a provisional, or temporary, credit to your account for the full amount of the disputed charge, for the two hundred seventeen dollars and seventy-six cents. This credit is not a permanent resolution, it's just so you don't have to pay for the charge while we investigate.

CUSTOMER: Oh, thank you. When will I see that credit?

AGENT: It typically posts to your account within ten business days, sometimes much sooner, maybe two or three days. You'll see it appear as a credit with a note that it's related to a dispute.

CUSTOMER: Okay, ten business days. So that should be before the payment is due. That's good.

AGENT: Yes, it should. And from there, we will contact the merchant's bank and provide them with the details of your claim. They then have a set amount of time to respond with there evidence. [crosstalk] Sorry, go ahead.

CUSTOMER: [crosstalk] So they have to prove I was there?

AGENT: Exactly. They would need to provide evidence that the charge is legitimate, like a signed receipt or an equipment rental agreement with your information on it. The merchant, Summit Ridge Ski Rentals, has until **July 4, 2026**, to respond to our request.

CUSTOMER: Wow, that’s a long time from now. July fourth?

AGENT: It is, yes. The regulations allow them a certain number of days, and it can take a while. But don't worry, the provisional credit will stay on your account during that whole time. If they fail to respond by **July 4, 2026**, or if they respond but can't provide sufficient proof, the dispute is closed in your favor, and that provisional credit automatically becomes permanent.

CUSTOMER: And what if they do have something? Like what if someone stole my number and forged my signature?

AGENT: If they provide evidence, we review it carefully. If it appears to be fraudulent, we would continue to fight the charge on your behalf. If they provide convincing evidence that the charge is valid, we would notify you and, unfortunately, the credit would be reversed. But in cases like this, where you've never been to the merchant, it's very, very rare for that to happen. The most likely outcome is that the merchant either won't respond or they'll accept the chargeback.

CUSTOMER: Okay. That makes sense. It's just so strange. I've never had this happen before. It makes you feel a little... violated, you know?

AGENT: I completely understand. It's an unsettling feeling. We’ll do everything we can to get this resolved for you. Just to confirm, I've filed dispute DSP-5976147 for the charge of $217.76 from Summit Ridge Ski Rentals. We've issued no permanent credit yet but a provisional credit will post within ten business days, and the merchant has until July 4th of this year to respond. Does that all sound correct?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s all correct. Thank you, Grace, you've been very helpful.

AGENT: You are most welcome, Ms. Okafor. Is there anything else at all I can assist you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, that was it. Thank you again.

AGENT: It was my pleasure. Thank you for being a customer, and have a wonderful rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye bye.

cust_synth_033:C03.body:
IVR: Thank you for calling Card Member Services. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. To ensure we can direct your call effectively, please listen to the following options. For questions about your balance, recent transactions, or to make a payment, press one. To report a card lost or stolen, press two. For questions about a dispute you have already filed, or to file a new dispute, press three. For all other inquiries, press four or stay on the line.

[tone]

IVR: Please have your card number ready. An agent will be with you shortly.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can manage your account 24/7 online at our secure website or by using our mobile app? Check your balance, pay your bill, and even lock your card, all from the palm of your hand. Thank you for your patience. We’ll be with you as soon as possible.

AGENT_1: Thank you for holding, you've reached Card Services, my name is Maria. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, my name is Ingrid Okafor.

AGENT_1: Hello, Ms. Okafor. How can I help you?

CUSTOMER: I'm calling to check on the status of a dispute. I filed it, um, a while ago. Last month, I think.

AGENT_1: Okay, I can help you with that. Can I get your full name again?

CUSTOMER: Ingrid Okafor. I-N-G-R-I-D. Okafor, O-K-A-F-O-R.

AGENT_1: Got it. And for security, can you please confirm the last four of your social for me?

CUSTOMER: Um, I don't really like giving that out over the phone. Is there another way?

AGENT_1: Of course. Let me see... I can ask you a few questions from your profile. Are you calling from the number we have on file?

CUSTOMER: I... don't think so? This is my work phone. The one on file is probably my cell.

AGENT_1: Okay, no problem. In that case, I... you know what, for disputes, I should probably get you over to the specialized department. They have a different set of verification questions and they'll have all the details on your case right in front of them. Would it be okay if I place you on a brief hold to transfer you?

CUSTOMER: Oh. Okay. Yes, I guess. I just want to know what's happening with it.

AGENT_1: I understand completely. They'll be able to give you the full picture. Please hold one moment.

[click]

HOLD MESSAGE: Traveling soon? Let us know your travel dates through the mobile app to ensure uninterrupted service. And remember, your card gives you access to exclusive travel benefits and no foreign transaction fees on purchases made abroad. Explore your benefits today.

AGENT: Thank you for holding, my name is Omar. I see you were transferred from Card Services regarding a dispute. I'm just pulling up your information now... okay. Hello, Ms. Okafor.

CUSTOMER: Yes, hello.

AGENT: I hope your day is going well. So, I can see the notes here. You're calling to check on a dispute for an online purchase you made last month?

CUSTOMER: No, it wasn't an online purchase. It was for a ski rental place. Summit Ridge Ski Rentals. I didn't even go skiing.

AGENT: Oh, my apologies. Thank you for clarifying that. Let me correct my understanding here. Summit Ridge Ski Rentals. Okay. I can see the dispute was opened... yes, about a month ago. Before we go any further, I do need to complete a quick security verification. Is that alright?

CUSTOMER: Yes, fine.

AGENT: Great. I'm not going to ask you for any full numbers, just to confirm a few things. Can you tell me the city and state you listed as your home address?

CUSTOMER: San Diego, California.

AGENT: Perfect. And we have an email address on file that was updated, uh, looks like a couple of weeks ago. Can you tell me what the part after the at-symbol is?

CUSTOMER: It should be example dot net.

AGENT: That is what I see here. Thank you for confirming that, Ms. Okafor. Your account is verified. So, you're calling about dispute DSP-5976147. Let me open that up. What was your specific question about it today?

CUSTOMER: Right, so, I saw a credit post to my account for the full amount, the two hundred seventeen dollars and seventy-six cents. It showed up, uh, let's see, the day before yesterday. So I just wanted to know, does that mean it's over? Is the dispute closed and the money is mine?

AGENT: That's an excellent question. Let me take a look at the transaction history. Yes, I see that. A provisional credit for $217.76. Okay. So, to answer your question, the short answer is no, the dispute is not officially closed yet.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Then what's the credit for?

AGENT: The provisional credit is something we issue to you so you're not out the funds while the investigation is ongoing. It's a temporary credit. We've sent the details of your claim to the merchant's bank, and now they have a period of time to respond—to either accept the chargeback or provide evidence that the charge was valid.

CUSTOMER: So... they could take the money back?

AGENT: If they provide compelling evidence, then yes, the credit could be reversed. But in many cases, especially if it's a clear error or fraud, the merchant doesn't respond and the credit becomes permanent. We just have to follow the process.

CUSTOMER: And how long does that process take? I feel like I've been waiting forever.

AGENT: I can understand your frustration. The regulations allow the merchant up to, well, it can be a couple of billing cycles, so it can take some time. I'm looking at the file now to see if there's any more specific timeline... one moment.

CUSTOMER: Uh-huh. Hold on a second, my brother is waving at me. What? Yes, I'm on the phone with them now. He wants to ask you something, is that okay? It's related.

AGENT: Um, sure, but I won't be able to discuss any account details that aren't yours, ma'am.

CUSTOMER: He knows. Here.

BROTHER: Yeah, hi. My name is Emeka. I was just telling her, I had almost the exact same thing happen on my card with you guys a few months ago. The charge was just, poof, gone, and the dispute was closed in like two weeks. Why is hers taking so long?

AGENT: Hello, sir. I appreciate the question, but every dispute is unique. The timeline can depend on the merchant, the amount, the reason for the dispute... a lot of factors. I really can't compare one case to another.

BROTHER: Right, but it's the same bank. I mean, my card is the one ending in 3192. It's a Prime card, just like hers. You'd think the process would be the same.

AGENT: I understand, but for privacy and security I can't pull up your account or discuss its history while on your sister's call. You would need to call the number on the back of your card and verify your own information.

BROTHER: Fine, fine, security. Can you give me a number to call back then? My number is 912-555-0606 if you need to...

AGENT: Sir, the best number to call is always the one printed on your card. I can't provide you with a direct line, but that number will get you to the right place.

BROTHER: Ugh. Okay. Ingrid, he's not telling me anything. Just, you know, ask him to hurry it up. This is ridiculous.

CUSTOMER: Okay, Emeka, thank you. Sorry about that, Omar. He means well.

AGENT: Not a problem at all, I completely understand. So, where were we? Ah, yes, the timeline. It really does just depend on the merchant's response. There isn't a firm date I can give you right now, I'm afraid.

CUSTOMER: So I just have to wait. That's... frustrating. I'm actually traveling soon, going to Nigeria to see my parents, and I just wanted this whole thing to be settled. You know, for peace of mind.

AGENT: I completely understand. It's always good to have finances squared away before a big trip. And while we're on the topic of travel, I see you have the Amazon Prime Visa. It's a great card for earning rewards, but just as a heads-up, if you're planning to use an ATM abroad, remember that's treated as a cash advance. There's a $15.00 fee per withdrawal and the interest starts right away at 31.49%.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Wow. Okay, fifteen dollars is a lot. Good to know. I wasn't planning on it, I usually just use my debit card for cash, but thank you for telling me.

AGENT: Of course. It's just one of those things people sometimes forget. And on the plus side, any travel you book through our portal can be paid for with points, and bookings start at just 1,000 points, so that's always an option for the future too.

CUSTOMER: Right. Okay, but back to this dispute. So there's no way to know? You can't tell me if the merchant has even looked at it? Can't you poke them or something?

AGENT: (chuckles softly) I wish I could, ma'am. The communication all happens through a formal, automated system between the banks. I can see that the request was sent and that we're waiting for a reply. That's the current status.

CUSTOMER: This is not helpful. I called about this over a month ago. I updated my email like you guys asked. I've done everything. I need to speak to a supervisor. Someone who can actually give me a real answer or at least a better idea of the timeline.

AGENT: I can certainly arrange for that. I can put in a request for a supervisor from the disputes team to give you a call back.

CUSTOMER: Okay. Yes. Please do that.

AGENT: Absolutely. And what's the best number for them to reach you at?

CUSTOMER: My office landline is probably best. It's... uh... nine one two, five five five, oh one three six. No, wait, that's the old line, we just moved desks. Sorry. It's nine one two, five five five, oh one six three.

AGENT: No problem at all. Let me read that back to you to be sure. That's nine one two, five five five, oh one six three.

CUSTOMER: Yes, that is correct.

AGENT: Perfect. I've noted that number down in your file. And so I can track this request properly, I'm opening a new case specifically for this callback request. The reference number for our conversation today is CASE-5177007.

CUSTOMER: Okay... CASE-5177007. Got it. And when will they call?

AGENT: I will have a supervisor call you back on that landline by Friday to discuss the dispute timeline in more detail. I have marked the request as urgent given how long you've been waiting for an update.

CUSTOMER: By this Friday? You promise? Because last time someone said they'd follow up and I never heard anything. That was about the email thing.

AGENT: I see that note, and I apologize for that lapse. Yes, I am personally submitting this request to my supervisor's queue. You will receive a call by Friday.

CUSTOMER: Okay. Okay, thank you, Omar. I appreciate that. That's all I need for now, then. Just... please make sure they call.

AGENT: I will, Ms. Okafor. I've documented everything. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, that's it. Thank you.

AGENT: You're very welcome. Thank you for calling Card Member Services, and I hope you have a wonderful trip.

CUSTOMER: Thanks. Bye.

cust_synth_033:C05.body:
Cx Ingrid Okafor came into the branch today, approx 11:15am. Seemed a little frustrated but was very pleasant.
Pulled her profile after standard CCK. ID verified.
Primary reason for visit: her Amazon Prime Visa card (*6824).

Cx states that for the past week or so, the chip on the card has been failing.
- It’s not being read at terminals.
- First time it happened was at the grocery store, had to swipe, held up the line, very embarrassing per cx.
- Has happened multiple times since. Sometimes the swipe works, sometimes it doesn't.
- She tried cleaning the chip w/ an alcohol wipe, her brother Emeka told her to try that, didn't help.
- Worried she’s going to get stuck somewhere unable to pay.
- Asked if this is a common problem. I told her it happens sometimes, cards get demagnetized or the chip just wears out over time.

Took a look at the card itself. No visible damage, no cracks or obvious scratches on the chip, but it does look a little worn. Looks like a classic chip failure.

While I was looking at her account, I noticed the recent case activity. Asked her if everything was sorted with that one charge she’d been looking into a while back.
- She lit up a bit, said "Oh, the ski rental thing? Yes, thank goodness."
- Said the provisional credit showed up, which she was happy about.
- Mentioned how weird it was, b/c she lives in San Diego and hasn't seen snow in years, let alone rented skis. Said it must have been some kind of data breach. I agreed it was likely.
- Cx mentioned that incident is what made her want to get paper statements again, just to have a hard copy to go over. She remembered getting an email about it and said she appreciated the quick response. Confirmed she received the itemized copy she'd requested. She said not yet, but she knows it can take a little time in the mail.
- This led to me verifying her contact info to make sure we have everything right for the new card shipment.
- Confirmed mailing address on file is correct.
- Confirmed email is ingrid.okafor92@example.net. I mentioned that I saw it had been updated not too long ago, just wanted to double-check it was the right one. She laughed and said "Yes, the one with the dot! I always forget the dot." So that seems fine.
- Also confirmed the callback number she’d provided before, the 912-555-0163 number. She confirmed that's her office line here, which is better to reach her at during the day than her cell. Good to know. She's visiting her brother Emeka for a few weeks from San Diego. Talked a little bit about the weather difference, she misses the dry California air.

Back to the card issue.
Advised cx that the best course of action is to just replace the card.
Explained the process:
- I will order a replacement card for her today.
- It will be a new Amazon Prime Visa, but it will have a new card number for security. The new card will be ending in *9995.
- It will be sent via standard USPS mail to her verified address on file.
- Should arrive in 5-7 business days. Advised her with mail sometimes being slow it could be more like 8 or 9, just to set expectations.
- MOST IMPORTANTLY: I advised her that her current card, *6824, will remain active and usable until she receives and activates the new card (*9995).
- So she can continue to use it for online purchases, or for swiping where it works. She was very relieved about this, said she has some automatic payments tied to it and was worried about them failing.
- I walked her through how to activate the new card once it arrives - either by calling the number on the sticker or by logging into her online banking profile.

Cx understood and agreed to the replacement.
Proceeded with card replacement workflow in the system.
- Selected Credit Card Services > Manage Card > Order Replacement.
- Reason code: Damaged/Non-functional Card.
- Typed in notes: "Per cx, chip no longer being read at POS terminals."
- System prompted to confirm mailing address, confirmed with cx again.
- Submitted the order.

Pasted system confirmation into the record:
REPLACEMENT CARD ORDERED FOR ACCT ENDING 6824.
NEW CARD NUMBER ENDING IN *9995.
DELIVERY TYPE: STANDARD MAIL (5-7 BUSINESS DAYS).
REASON: DAMAGED - CHIP MALFUNCTION.
EXISTING CARD REMAINS ACTIVE UNTIL NEW CARD IS ACTIVATED BY CUSTOMER.

Showed the confirmation screen to the cx (not the note, just the user-facing screen).
She asked again just to be sure, "So if I buy something on Amazon tonight, the old card will still work?" I confirmed yes, absolutely. Online, phone orders, recurring bills, anything where you don't need the physical chip will work 100% fine until she activates the new one. She said "perfect."

She seemed happy with the resolution. Thanked me for being so helpful. We chatted for another minute while I was finishing the notes. She mentioned her brother is trying to get her to move here from San Diego but she doesn't think she can handle the humidity. A very friendly cx.

Follow-up:
- Set a task to f/u w/ cx in approx. 8 business days to ensure new card *9995 arrived safely. Will use office number 912-555-0163.
- No other f/u required. End of interaction.

CUSTOMER: Again? But you're calling me.

AGENT: I know, and I appreciate your patience. It's a standard security procedure on any new connection, just to ensure I am speaking with the account holder. Can I please have you confirm your full name for me?

CUSTOMER: Ingrid Okafor.

CUSTOMER: San Diego, California.

AGENT: Perfect. And just the last piece, could you provide the last four digits of your Social Security Number?

CUSTOMER: It's [REDACTED].

AGENT: Got it. Thank you so much for that. Okay, I have the account pulled back up here and I see all my notes from our previous conversation. I also see the case file I started for you, CASE-… sorry, I have the reference file here to track this. So, it looks like we were right in the middle of activating your new Amazon Prime Visa card.

CUSTOMER: Yes, exactly. The one you sent in the mail. I went to the branch because my old one, the chip just stopped working out of nowhere. It was so embarrassing, I was at the grocery store.

AGENT: Right, yes, I see the note here from your branch visit back in May. They ordered the replacement for you, and it looks like you received it. So, just to confirm, you have the new card ending in **** 9995 with you now?

CUSTOMER: I do, yes. It's right here.

AGENT: Excellent. My brother was even here, he heard it. Nobody ever called. It’s just… it’s frustrating. You feel like you’re shouting into a void sometimes.

CUSTOMER: Okay, thank you. I appreciate that, Tom. Um, actually, while I have you… can I ask something else? I was just looking at my account online before I called you the first time, and I saw a late fee.

AGENT: A late fee? Okay, let me take a look here for you. Just one moment while I switch screens… I’m looking at your most recent statement now… ah. Yes, I do see that charge.

CUSTOMER: I don’t understand why it’s there. I paid the bill. I always pay the bill. I set a reminder and everything.

AGENT: Hmm. Let me see the payment history. Okay, I see the payment. It looks like… it looks like the payment was posted one day after the official due date, Ms. Okafor. Sometimes with electronic payments, depending on when you submit it, it can take a business day or two to fully process and post to the account.

CUSTOMER: But I paid it on the day. I know I did. This is what I’m talking about, it’s always some little thing.

AGENT: I understand your frustration, I really do. And I can see from your history that you have a perfect payment record going back years. You’ve never had a late fee before. So, here’s what I’m going to do for you. As a one-time courtesy, given your excellent history with us, I’m going to go ahead and waive that thirty-eight dollars late fee for you right now. The system notes that a fee waiver for the $38.00 amount can only be applied once every 12 months, but I'm happy to do that for you right now to resolve this.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Really?

AGENT: Absolutely. Let me just process that… okay. I’ve submitted the credit. You should see that fee disappear from your pending balance within 24 hours, and it will be reflected as a credit on your next statement.

CUSTOMER: Wow. Okay, thank you. Thank you very much.

AGENT: I see that. I’m very sorry that wasn't sent. I’m going to re-submit that request for you right now. I'm just confirming the address on file… it’s a residence in San Diego, zip code 92101. Is that still correct?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s correct.

AGENT: Okay. I’ve put in a new, expedited request for that statement copy. It should go out in tomorrow’s mail, so you should have it in three to five business days. I’ve also noted the failure of the original request.

CUSTOMER: Thank you, Tom. It feels like we’re actually getting things done now.

AGENT: That’s my goal, Ms. Okafor. Happy to help. So, are you ready to finally activate this new card and put this all behind us?

CUSTOMER: Yes, please. Let’s do it.

AGENT: Alright. So you have the new card, the one ending in **** 9995.

CUSTOMER: Yes.

AGENT: Okay. On the back of the card, in the signature panel, there is a three-digit security code. Could you please read that code to me?

CUSTOMER: Okay, let me get my glasses… hold on. It’s so small. Okay. The code is [REDACTED].

AGENT: Thank you. I’m entering that now… one moment please, the system is just verifying… Don’t hang up…

CUSTOMER: I won’t.

AGENT: Almost there… Okay! Success. Your new Amazon Prime Visa card ending in **** 9995 has been successfully activated. It is ready for you to use immediately.

CUSTOMER: Oh, thank goodness. Finally.

AGENT: And just so you are aware, this activation process has automatically and permanently deactivated your old card, the one ending in **** 6824. So you can go ahead and cut that one up and dispose of it.

CUSTOMER: Perfect. That’s the one with the broken chip anyway, so good riddance. So the new one is ready to go? I can go use it for lunch?

AGENT: You certainly can. It’s fully active. You’ll also want to make sure you update your card information for any automatic payments you have set up, you know, for subscriptions or online retailers, since the card number and expiration date have changed.

CUSTOMER: Right, right. My streaming services. I always forget that part. Thank you for the reminder.

AGENT: Of course. So, to recap our call today: we have successfully activated your new card ending in **** 9995, we’ve deactivated the old card ending in **** 6824, I have waived the recent late fee as a courtesy, and I’ve re-submitted your request for a mailed statement copy. Was there anything else at all I could help you with today, Ms. Okafor?

CUSTOMER: No, I think… I think that’s everything. You’ve been very helpful, Tom. Much better than my last few experiences, I have to say.

AGENT: I’m very glad I could help turn things around for you. Thank you again for your patience with the dropped call earlier. We appreciate your business. If there’s nothing else, I’ll let you get on with your day.

CUSTOMER: Okay, great. Thank you again.

AGENT: You're welcome. Have a wonderful day, Ms. Okafor. Goodbye.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye.

cust_synth_033:C11.body:
Customer Ingrid Okafor came into the branch today around 2:30 PM. Seemed to be in a good mood, just had a regular inquiry. I greeted her at the door and brought her over to my desk. I pulled up her profile after verifying her identity with her driver's license and her Amazon Prime Visa card (*9995). I confirmed the address on file in San Diego was still current, which she said it was. Everything looked good on my end, no flags or alerts on the account. SSN and DOB verification passed, system shows [REDACTED] for both.

She started by saying she needed to get a cashier's check. She said it was for a security deposit on a small office space she's thinking of renting for her freelance work. She wasn't sure of the exact process, how long it takes, or what the fees were. I explained that we could draft it right here, it would only take a few minutes. I walked her through the fee schedule for the check and explained that the funds would be withdrawn from her checking account immediately and held by the bank, which is why landlords prefer them. She nodded and said that made sense. She was pulling up the details on her phone, looking for the exact amount and the name of the payee.

While she was scrolling through her phone, she looked up and said, "Actually, you know what, while I'm here and you have my account open, I had a totally unrelated question if that's okay." I told her of course. This is when she shifted topics and asked about the process for closing an account with us. She immediately followed up, very clearly, and I am quoting her directly here: "I am NOT closing the account, I just want to know what the steps would be." She sort of laughed and said she was doing some "financial housekeeping" and trying to understand all her options with her various accounts at different institutions. She added, "It's not like I'm moving to another country or anything, I just like to be prepared."

I acknowledged that and told her it's a smart question to ask. I did a quick review of her profile while we were talking, noting her long-standing relationship with the bank and her card activity. To provide some retention value, I mentioned that I saw we were recently able to resolve that dispute for her from the winter. She smiled and said, "Oh yeah, the ski rental place! I was so glad that got sorted out. I never even used the equipment." I told her we were happy to help and that's part of the value we try to provide. Seeing the opening, I then mentioned that for our long-term customers, we always want to make sure the relationship is working for them and that we sometimes have promotions available. I said something like, "For example, just as an FYI, we're running a promotion right now where you could get a $200.00 statement credit just for setting up a new qualifying direct deposit. It's just something to keep in mind." I stressed it was just an example of the kinds of things we offer. She seemed interested, said "Oh, that's good to know, thank you," but didn't ask to sign up.

I then walked her through the hypothetical account closure process. I explained that she'd want to make sure all automatic payments and deposits were moved, that all pending transactions were cleared, and that the balance was brought to zero. I explained she could do that by withdrawing the funds or having a final check mailed to her address on file, which I confirmed again is the one in San Diego. I also noted that her Amazon Prime Visa (*9995) is linked to her checking account and we'd have to discuss how she'd want to handle that if she were to ever close the deposit account. She listened intently and thanked me, saying "Okay, great. That's exactly what I needed to know. Very clear. But yeah, not happening anytime soon."

She then found the information on her phone and we went back to the original request. "Okay, so, about that cashier's check," she said. The payee was a property management company and she had the exact dollar amount ready. I confirmed the spelling of the payee name twice and verified the funds were available in her checking account. I initiated the transaction in the system, had her sign the withdrawal slip and the request form, and printed the check. I presented it to her in a bank envelope along with her receipt. She checked the name and amount and said it was perfect. I asked if there was anything else I could help with, and she said no, that was everything. She thanked me again for my time and for answering her "random question." I told her it was my pleasure and to have a great rest of the week. She left the branch around 3:05 PM. Overall a very pleasant and straightforward interaction. I have noted the retention conversation in the system for future reference.

Follow-up:
Action Taken: Issued cashier's check from checking account per customer's request. Answered procedural questions about account closure.
Next Steps: No immediate follow-up required. Customer explicitly stated she is not planning to close her account.
Opportunity: Customer was informed of a current promotion (a $200.00 statement credit for new direct deposit). She was polite but non-committal. May be a point of conversation if she calls or visits again in the next few months. No further action needed at this time.

IVR: Thank you for calling Chase. Your call may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance.
IVR: To continue in English, press one. Para continuar en español, oprima dos.
IVR: Please say or enter your sixteen-digit card number.
CUSTOMER: Representative.
IVR: I'm sorry, I didn't get that. To report a card lost or stolen, press one. For questions about your balance or a recent transaction, press two. To speak with a customer service specialist, press zero or stay on the line.
IVR: Please hold while I connect you to the next available agent. Your estimated wait time is three to five minutes.

HOLD MESSAGE: [upbeat instrumental music] Did you know you can earn a $200.00 statement credit after you spend five hundred dollars on purchases in your first three months from account opening? Learn more about the Chase Freedom Unlimited card at chase dot com. That's a $200.00 statement credit. Visit chase dot com to learn more. [upbeat instrumental music continues] We value your time and will be with you shortly. You can also manage your account, pay your bill, and check recent transactions at chase dot com or in the Chase mobile app.

AGENT: Thank you for holding, you've reached Chase Card Services, my name is Marcus. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with today?

CUSTOMER: Uh, yes, hello. My name is Andre Haddad.

AGENT: Hello, Mr. Haddad. How can I help you?

CUSTOMER: I'm, uh, looking at my statement here, my online statement, and there's a charge that I do not recognize at all. It's a pretty big one.

AGENT: Okay, I can definitely look into that for you. To make sure I'm accessing the correct account and for your security, can I just ask you to verify a few things for me?

CUSTOMER: Yes, sure.

AGENT: Great. Can you please confirm the home city and state that we have on file for you?

CUSTOMER: It's Atlanta, Georgia.

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. And just to fully verify, I'm going to send a temporary security code to the email address we have on file, it starts with andreh21 and ends in example dot net. Can you let me know when you receive that and read the code back to me?

CUSTOMER: Okay, one second. Let me pull up my email. I have so many windows open. Okay... okay, got it. The code is... um... 7-3-0-1-9-4.

AGENT: Thank you very much, Mr. Haddad. Okay, I have your account pulled up here, I see the Chase Slate Edge card ending in 4628.

CUSTOMER: That's the one. Yes.

AGENT: Alright. And you said there was a charge you didn't recognize. Can you tell me a bit more about it? The amount or the merchant name?

CUSTOMER: Yeah it's for, uh, let me see. It's for six hundred two dollars and sixty-four cents. I just... I don't remember spending that much money anywhere recently. I think... I think it might have been at Burlington? We were there last weekend but I definitely didn't spend six hundred dollars. Not even close.

AGENT: Okay, I'm looking at your recent transactions now. Six hundred two dollars and sixty-four cents. I see a few charges from last weekend but nothing for that specific amount. What was the date of the charge?

CUSTOMER: Uhhhhh hold on. The state meant is just... it's a mess. So many little things. Let me sort it by amount.
WIFE: (in background) Andre, are you still on with the bank? Don't forget to ask them about the flowers!
CUSTOMER: Yes, Elara, I'm on it right now, just give me a second. (to agent) Sorry about that. Okay, I'm finding it here. It's... oh. Oh, wait a minute. It's not Burlington. My mistake. It says... Harbor Lights Florist?

AGENT: Harbor Lights Florist, you said?

CUSTOMER: Yes. Harbor Lights Florist. I have never, ever heard of that place. A florist? For six hundred bucks? No way. Absolutely not.

AGENT: Okay, I see the transaction now. It posted on February 28th. A charge from Harbor Lights Florist for six hundred two dollars and sixty-four cents.

CUSTOMER: February 28th... nope. That wasn't me. I didn't buy any flowers, my wife didn't buy any flowers, nobody in this house bought six hundred dollars worth of flowers. That's insane. Is that even a real place? Harbor Lights Forest?

AGENT: It says... F-L-O-R-I-S-T. Florist. Yes, it appears to be a legitimate merchant. But you're certain you didn't make this purchase or authorize anyone else to make it?

CUSTOMER: One hundred percent certain. A thousand percent. There is a zero percent chance I made that charge.

AGENT: Do you currently have your physical card with you, Mr. Haddad?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it's right here in my wallet. It hasn't left my sight.

AGENT: Okay. And you haven't shared your card details with anyone or entered them on a website you didn't recognize?

CUSTOMER: No. No. I'm very careful about that. This is completely out of the blue. I need this charge removed. This has to be fraud.

AGENT: I understand your concern, Mr. Haddad, and I'm going to open a dispute for this transaction right away. I just need to ask a few more procedural questions, okay?

CUSTOMER: Yes, okay, whatever you need.

AGENT: Thank you. So, just to be clear for the record, you do not recognize the merchant Harbor Lights Florist, and you did not authorize this charge for six hundred two dollars and sixty-four cents. Is that correct?

CUSTOMER: That is correct. Absolutely.

AGENT: Okay. I'm opening a fraud dispute now. This is going to generate two reference numbers for you. The first one is for this call, sort of an internal case file for our conversation. The second one is for the dispute itself, which is what you'll use to track the investigation into the charge. Do you have a pen and paper handy?

CUSTOMER: Uh, yeah, just a second. [inaudible shuffling] Okay, go ahead.

AGENT: Alright. The case number for our call today is CASE-8894325.

CUSTOMER: CASE... dash... eight eight nine four... three two five. Got it.

AGENT: And the dispute number, this is the important one, is DSP-2174159.

CUSTOMER: D... S... P... dash... two one seven... four one five nine. Okay. DSP-2174159.

AGENT: Perfect. So, what happens now is we will investigate this on your behalf. We will contact the merchant's bank to get more information about the charge. In the meantime, we will issue a provisional credit to your account for the full disputed amount.

CUSTOMER: A provisional credit? So you're putting the money back?

AGENT: Yes, for the time being. The credit for the six hundred two dollars and sixty-four cents should appear on your account within the next, uh, it's usually within ten business days. Sometimes it's much faster, maybe two or three, but we say ten just to be safe. While the charge is in dispute, you are not responsible for paying that portion of your balance.

CUSTOMER: Okay, good. That's a relief. So what happens then?

AGENT: Well, the merchant—in this case, Harbor Lights Florist—will have a set amount of time to respond to the dispute and provide proof that the charge was valid. You know, a signed receipt, proof of delivery to your address, something like that. They have until July 1, 2026 to provide that documentation.

CUSTOMER: July 1st? Wow, that's a long time from now.

AGENT: It is, yes. These things can sometimes take a while, depending on how quickly the merchant and their bank respond. But you don't need to worry about that deadline. For you, the important thing is the provisional credit. If the merchant doesn't respond by July 1, 2026, or if they can't provide valid proof, the dispute is closed in your favor, and that provisional credit becomes permanent.

AGENT: No, no that makes sense. So you're saying I don't have to pay it right now?

AGENT: That's correct, you will not have to pay the disputed amount. If for some reason the merchant *does* provide compelling evidence that the charge is legitimate, we would contact you immediately and the provisional credit might be reversed, but that only happens if they can prove it was you, and from what you're telling me, that seems unlikely.

CUSTOMER: It's impossible. They won't find anything because it didn't happen. [crosstalk] So I just wait to see the credit show up?

AGENT: Exactly. You just keep an eye on your account for that credit to post. And if you don't see it within ten business days, please give us a call back and reference your dispute number. But you should be all set. I've submitted the dispute now. Is there anything else I can help you with today, Mr. Haddad? Perhaps another transaction you had a question about?

CUSTOMER: No, that was the only one. It just... it really jumped out at me. Six hundred dollars... phew. Okay, so, just to be sure, the case is CASE-8894325 and the dispute is DSP-2174159.

AGENT: That is absolutely correct.

CUSTOMER: And provisional credit in ten business days, and the charge is from Harbor Lights Florist.

AGENT: Yes, you've got it all. I've also added detailed notes to your account about our conversation.

CUSTOMER: Okay. Well, thank you, Marcus. You've been very helpful. I was pretty stressed out about this.

AGENT: It's my pleasure to help, Mr. Haddad. I'm glad we could get this process started for you. We take these things very seriously.

CUSTOMER: I appreciate that. Alright, well, I guess that's everything then.

AGENT: It is. Thank you for being a Chase customer, and I hope you have a much better rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Thanks again. Bye.

AGENT: Goodbye.

From: Sofia Doyle <sofia.doyle73@example.net>
To: Card Services <support@bank.example>
Date: Tue, Aug 9, 2026 at 11:21 AM
Subject: Two things to update on my account

Hello,

I need to make a couple of changes to my account and I’m hoping you can help me via email as I’m in back-to-back meetings all day.

First, I need to change the primary email address you have on file for me. This one (`sofia.doyle73@example.net`) is an old personal one and I’m trying to consolidate everything. I have a new one I’d like to use for all bank communications going forward.

Second, I unfortunately need to cancel a travel notice I set up a while ago. It was for a trip to Reykjavik, Iceland in mid-August on my Chase Slate Edge card (*6065). Some unforeseen circumstances have come up and the trip has been postponed indefinitely, so I won't be needing the notice anymore. I don't want any legitimate charges here in Charlotte to get accidentally blocked while the notice is active.

On a positive note, I wanted to say thank you to whoever helped with that dispute over the luggage charge a few weeks back. It was a relief to see that finally get resolved in my favor. Your team has always been very helpful, even going back to when my new card was activated and the call kept dropping, you guys were great about calling me right back.

Please let me know what you need from me to get these two things taken care of.

Thanks,
Sofia Doyle

I look forward to your reply.

Sincerely,

Keisha
Card Services Specialist
Case ID: CASE-1453067

cust_synth_017:C05.body:
Cx Andre Haddad in branch today approx 11:15am. Not a local cx, lives in Atlanta, GA, just visiting the area. Pleasant guy, very patient.

- Cx presented his Chase Slate Edge card (*4628) which was in very rough shape. Looked like it had been through the wash about a hundred times. The magnetic stripe was completely shredded, silver and peeling. A whole corner of the card was also physically snapped off, right through the plastic.
- He said it's been getting harder and harder to use for a while, lots of swipe errors, but today it finally gave up the ghost. Said he tried to buy a sandwich and the reader just wouldn't take it. Laughed and said "it wasn't even twenty bucks, you'd think it could handle that." Said the chip still works fine, but the swipe failure was the last straw for him.

- Pulled up his profile, performed full CCK. Verified name, address on file in Atlanta, GA. Also verified email on file andre.haddad47@example.net and callback number 502-555-0923. Cx confirmed all info was correct. He mentioned he was glad the right email was on there, remembered having to change it a while back b/c we had an old one for him. Good to see the updates stuck.

- While the system was loading I chatted w/ him. He's very easy to talk to. He vaguely mentioned having another issue a few months ago, said something about a really weird charge showing up on his statement. Per cx, it was a big charge for flowers, and he said "my husband Gustavo would have had a heart attack if he thought I spent that much without telling him." IVR: Thank you for calling Chase. Your call may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance. To continue in English, press one. Para continuar en español, oprima dos.

IVR: Please say or enter your full 16-digit card number.

IVR: I didn't get that. Please say or enter your full 16-digit card number.

IVR: Okay. Using the keypad on your phone, please enter the last four digits of your social security number.

IVR: Thank you. Please tell me in a few words what you're calling about. You can say things like "check my balance," "report a lost card," or "dispute a charge."

CUSTOMER: Check on a dispute.

IVR: Okay, I can help with that. One moment while I connect you to a specialist. Please be aware that wait times are currently longer than usual. We appreciate your patience.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can manage your account, pay your bill, and even redeem rewards right from the Chase Mobile app? It's the fastest and easiest way to stay in control of your finances. Visit the app store and download the Chase Mobile app today. We'll be right with you.

AGENT: Thank you for holding, my name is Carlos. I understand you're calling to check on a dispute. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with?

CUSTOMER: Hi, this is Andre Haddad.

AGENT: Hello, Mr. Haddad. For your security, I just need to verify a few details. I'm sending a one-time code to the mobile number we have on file. Can you please read that back to me when you receive it?

CUSTOMER: Uh, sure. Hold on. Okay, I got the text. It's... just a sec... 7-3-0-1-5-5.

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. That's verified. So, you're calling about an existing dispute? Do you happen to have the dispute number handy?

CUSTOMER: I do, yes. It's DSP-2174159.

AGENT: Okay, D-S-P-2-1-7-4-1-5-9. Let me just pull that up. This can take a moment, the system is a little slow today.

CUSTOMER: It's always a little slow.

AGENT: (chuckles) You're not wrong there. Okay... I'm seeing it here. It's for a charge of $602.64, is that correct?

CUSTOMER: That's the one. I saw a credit for that amount posted, a provisional credit I guess you call it. It showed up the day before yesterday. I just want to know what that means. Like, is it over? Is the money mine? Or can the merchant still fight it?

AGENT: That's a great question, Mr. Haddad. The provisional credit means that while we investigate, you don't have to pay for that charge. It's a temporary credit. It doesn't mean the dispute is closed.

CUSTOMER: Right, that's what I thought. So what's the timeline? How long does this investigation take? I called about this over a month ago.

AGENT: I understand your concern. These investigations can take some time, as we have to give the merchant a fair opportunity to respond with their side of the story. For the specific timeline and the current status of the merchant response, I'll need to transfer you to our specialized disputes team. They have access to more detailed information than I do. Is that okay?

CUSTOMER: I guess. I just feel like I'm going to get bounced around.

AGENT: I'll make a warm transfer, so you won't have to repeat everything. I'll brief the next agent on your call. Please hold one moment.

CUSTOMER: Okay.

HOLD MESSAGE: Your financial health is important to us. With Chase Credit Journey, you can check your credit score for free, without impacting your credit. Get alerts for critical changes and learn what's affecting your score. It's free for everyone, not just Chase customers. Log in to your account to get started. An agent will be with you shortly.

AGENT: Hello Mr. Haddad, thank you so much for your patience. My name is Grace, and I see you're calling from Atlanta. Carlos has filled me in.

CUSTOMER: Hi Grace. Yes, I am. And you know what I'm calling about?

AGENT: I do. I'm looking at the notes here. You're calling about dispute DSP-2174159, regarding a charge from Burlington for $602.64. You saw the provisional credit post and you're wondering what the next steps and timeline are for the investigation. Is that all correct?

CUSTOMER: Almost. The merchant wasn't Burlington. It was a place called Harbor Lights Florist. I might have said Burlington when I first called way back when because I was just guessing, but it was definitely the florist. The amount is right, though.

AGENT: Oh, my apologies for that! Thank you for the correction. I see it noted correctly here in the dispute details, Harbor Lights Florist. I must have misread Carlos's summary note. I'm sorry about that. Let me get into the actual dispute file, that's the source of truth.

CUSTOMER: It's fine. So, can you tell me what's going on with it?

AGENT: Of course. I'm looking at the file now. So, yes, the provisional credit for the full amount of $602.64 was posted to your Chase Slate Edge card, the one ending in 4628. That happened the day before yesterday, as you said. That's our standard procedure. Now, as for the timeline, we have sent the details of your claim to the merchant's bank. They now have a period of time to respond with any evidence they might have, like a signed receipt or proof of delivery.

CUSTOMER: And how long do they have?

AGENT: It can vary, but typically they have up to 45 days from the time we notify them. Since we initiated this process after your call last month, we should be hearing something back relatively soon.

CUSTOMER: So it could be another month? This seems crazy for a charge I never made.

AGENT: I completely understand your frustration, Mr. Haddad. The timelines are regulated to ensure both parties have a chance to present their case. We do everything we can to move it along. I can see the original case was opened back in early March, so we are well into that window.

CUSTOMER: Okay. While you're looking at my account, I just have another general question. I have some points... I travel for work sometimes. How does that work if I go overseas?

AGENT: A great question. With your Slate Edge card, you can certainly use it for purchases abroad. Just as a heads-up, since you have the Slate Edge card, do be aware that there's a 3% foreign transaction fee on any purchases made outside the US.

CUSTOMER: Right, okay. Good to know. And what about my points? I see a balance in the app.

AGENT: Let me see here... Yes, you have a good amount saved up. And I see you have... 18,858 points on your Slate Edge card. Just so you know for future reference, if you ever wanted to redeem those for a statement credit, you need a minimum of 5,000 points, and once you transfer them to one of our airline partners, they can't be moved back. Just a little tip.

CUSTOMER: Okay, thanks. I don't really use them, but good to know. Back to this dispute... what happens if the merchant responds?

AGENT: If they provide compelling evidence that the charge is valid, we would have to review it. If they don't respond, or if their evidence isn't sufficient, the dispute is typically found in your favor and the provisional credit becomes permanent.

CUSTOMER: And you'll let me know? By email? I updated my email with you guys a few weeks ago, I hope it's the right one. `andre.haddad47@example.net`.

AGENT: Let me check that for you... Yes, I see `andre.haddad47@example.net` is the primary email on the account. We would send all correspondence there.

CUSTOMER: Hold on one second, Grace. My husband is trying to talk to me. What? No, I'm on the phone with them now.

HUSBAND: (muffled in background) Ask them about my card! The replacement!

CUSTOMER: He wants to know about his replacement card.

AGENT: I'm sorry, sir, but for security and privacy, I can only discuss an account with the verified account holder. Is he an authorized user on your account?

CUSTOMER: No, he has his own account. He's just being impatient. Gustavo, she can't talk to me about your account.

HUSBAND: (louder) Well can you ask them about my card too? Just tell them Gustavo Haddad. The card ending in 1675. I'm still waiting on that replacement.

AGENT: Sir, I really am unable to access or discuss his account details with you. He would need to call in from the number on his file and verify his own identity. I'm sure you understand.

CUSTOMER: Yes, I know. Sorry about that. He's just... ugh.

HUSBAND: (in background) Well give them my number in case they need to call me about it. It's 502-555-0860.

CUSTOMER: He can call himself. Sorry, Grace. He's gone now. Anyway, back to my issue. I don't want to just wait for an email that I might miss. Can someone actually call me with an update?

AGENT: We can certainly add a note to the file to request a callback. What's the best number to reach you?

CUSTOMER: Yes, my office landline. It's... let me think... 502-555-0932. Oh, wait, sorry, I always do that. My old number. The correct one is 502-555-0923.

AGENT: No problem at all. Let me read that back to you. The best callback number is 502-555-0923.

CUSTOMER: That's the one. And I want a real update. I want to know when I can expect this to be over. Can't you escalate this? It's a lot of money and it's been a long time.

AGENT: I hear you, Mr. Haddad, and I can tell this is a priority. Given the age of the dispute, I think an escalation is warranted. What I can do is open a case to have a supervisor review the dispute timeline for you. They can take a deeper look and see if there's any way to expedite the process or at least get you a more concrete status. They will call back on the landline you just provided.

CUSTOMER: Okay, and when will they call? I don't want to wait another week.

AGENT: I will put in the request with a high priority. The standard turnaround for a supervisor callback is two to three business days. I can promise you'll receive that call back by Friday at the latest.

CUSTOMER: By this coming Friday?

AGENT: Yes, absolutely. By Friday.

CUSTOMER: Okay. That's better. At least it's something.

AGENT: I've documented our entire conversation and your request for an escalated review. I'm submitting that now. The reference number for today's call and this new request is CASE-5955263.

CUSTOMER: Okay, let me write that down. C-A-S-E... 5-9-5-5-2-6-3. Got it. And you're sure they'll call that number? The one ending in 923?

AGENT: Yes, I have it right here in the notes. A supervisor will call 502-555-0923 by Friday regarding dispute DSP-2174159.

CUSTOMER: Alright, Grace. Thank you. You've been more helpful than the last guy.

AGENT: You are very welcome, Mr. Haddad. I'm glad I could assist and get that escalation started for you. Is there anything else at all I can help you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, that's it. Just please make sure they call.

AGENT: I've put the request in and marked it as urgent. You'll be hearing from us. Thank you for being a Chase customer, and I hope you have a wonderful rest of your weekend.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye.

AGENT: Goodbye.
